target.title: fix(mattermost): reject oversized websocket events
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators connected to a buggy or hostile self-hosted Mattermost server could have the monitor WebSocket client buffer an oversized event payload before the `ws` client rejected it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now sets a 4 MiB inbound WebSocket payload cap on the default `ws` client. Mattermost WebSocket traffic is documented as JSON event envelopes, and Mattermost server source permits large post props/cards, so this stays above a valid posted-event envelope while avoiding the upstream `ws` client default of 100 MiB for this monitor path.

Mattermost API docs: https://developers.mattermost.com/api-documentation/

Mattermost post validation source: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/server/public/model/post.go

## User Impact

Mattermost users keep receiving normal channel activity, while runaway or hostile WebSocket frames fail fast with standard payload-too-large behavior instead of being buffered up to the much larger client default.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts`: 11 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig tsconfig.json extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.ts extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-websocket.test.ts`: passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD`: passed.

target.title: fix(browser): bound client-fetch JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`fetchHttpJson` in the browser control transport reads JSON response bodies
with an unbounded `await res.json()` call on the success path. A misbehaving
browser-service endpoint that returns an oversized JSON payload can exhaust
gateway memory.

The error path in the same function already handles this — it reads error
bodies through `readResponseWithLimit` with a 16 KiB cap. The success path was
simply missed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw `res.json()` with the already-imported `readResponseWithLimit`
helper, using a 16 MiB cap. The stream is cancelled on overflow.

## Evidence

`readResponseWithLimit` is already imported (line 9) and used on the error
path (line 275) in the same file. The fix applies the same helper to the
success path.

```diff
@@ -277,7 +278,8 @@ async function fetchHttpJson<T>(
-    return (await res.json()) as T;
+    const body = await readResponseWithLimit(res, BROWSER_RESPONSE_LIMIT_BYTES);
+    return JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(body)) as T;
```

Real behavior proof — `readResponseWithLimit` rejects an oversized body:

```text
$ node --import tsx proof-browser-bound.mjs
ok: 11-byte response read successfully (cap: 256)
overflow: 512 bytes with 256-byte cap
OVERFLOW CAUGHT: Content too large: 512 bytes (limit: 256 bytes)
PASS
```

Format check:

```text
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/browser/src/browser/client-fetch.ts
Finished in 2ms on 1 files using 1 threads.
```

Note: `/snapshot` requests use the CDP transport, not `fetchHttpJson` /
`fetchBrowserJson`, so the snapshot `maxChars=0` uncapped contract is not
affected by this change.

target.title: fix(acp): use Object.hasOwn instead of in operator in printSessionUpdate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `printSessionUpdate` helper in `src/acp/client.ts:75` uses the `in` operator to check for `sessionUpdate` on the notification update object. The `in` operator traverses the prototype chain, so it would match inherited properties — though unlikely in practice, `Object.hasOwn()` is the more correct semantic for own-property checks.

## Changes

- **`src/acp/client.ts`** — replace `!("sessionUpdate" in update)` with `!Object.hasOwn(update, "sessionUpdate")` (1 line)

## Evidence

Direct behavior probe — `Object.hasOwn` vs `in` operator equivalence for own-property checks:

```text
$ node -e "..."
=== Object.hasOwn vs in operator equivalence ===
Own property - Object.hasOwn: true
Own property - in operator: true
Missing property - Object.hasOwn: false
Missing property - in operator: false
Inherited only - Object.hasOwn: false
Inherited only - in operator: true

The ACP update object has sessionUpdate as own property,
so Object.hasOwn and in operator are equivalent here.
Object.hasOwn is safer: it would NOT match a prototype-injected property.
```

The ACP SDK contract requires and validates the `sessionUpdate` discriminator as an own property. This change is purely mechanical and behavior-preserving.

## Related

N/A (self-contained code hygiene improvement)

target.title: feat(status): surface last compaction outcome in /status
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Compaction attempts already get classified into stable reason buckets (`classifyCompactionReason`: `summary_failed`, `timeout`, `guard_blocked`, `provider_error_4xx/5xx`, `below_threshold`, …), but that classification only exists in transient log lines and the in-turn `/compact` reply. Once the turn is over, the outcome is gone: `/status` shows a bare `🧹 Compactions: N` counter, and an operator who wasn't watching the live session cannot answer "did the last compaction work, and if not, why?" — even though failing or perpetually-skipped compaction is a common root cause of the context-overflow symptoms they are trying to diagnose.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reason classification, the persisted `SessionEntry`, and the `/status` renderer all already exist — the missing piece is persisting the last classified outcome onto the session entry the way sibling diagnostics already do (`memoryFlushLastFailedAt` / `memoryFlushLastFailureError` follow exactly this pattern).

This change adds three optional `SessionEntry` fields (`lastCompactionAt`, `lastCompactionOutcome`, `lastCompactionReason`) and stamps them at the seams where a compaction attempt concludes with a known outcome:

- **successful compactions**: `incrementCompactionCount` (manual `/compact`, preflight/budget compaction), the post-run reconcile handler (live-run auto compactions), the gateway `sessions.compact` RPC (both the LLM branch and the `maxLines` transcript-trim branch), and the CLI-session compaction/finalize paths
- **failed/skipped attempts**: a new `recordCompactionOutcome` helper (same store mechanics as `incrementCompactionCount`, with `preserveActivity: true` so a failed attempt does not count as session activity), called from manual `/compact` and the preflight/budget compaction path; the gateway compact RPC stamps the same fields directly in its existing `updateSessionStore` mutations (LLM failed/skipped branch and trim no-op paths), where the store write already lives

Consistency guards (all verified by focused tests):

- **No resurrection**: a metadata-only failed/skipped stamp never creates a row, in memory or on disk — a session deleted/reset while compaction was in flight stays deleted (`recordCompactionOutcome` passes no `fallbackEntry` and mirrors to memory only after the persisted patch confirms the row exists).
- **No out-of-order regression**: every writer that captures its timestamp before awaiting the store writer applies the stamp through `isCompactionStampCurrent`, so a delayed older attempt cannot overwrite a newer outcome; full-entry finalizer patches (`updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun`, `recordCliCompactionInStore`) strip the pre-run `lastCompaction*` snapshot so merging stale metadata cannot roll the fields back.
- Only the classified bucket is persisted — raw provider error text stays out of durable session metadata.

`/status` then renders a null-conditional suffix on the existing counter line:

```
🧹 Compactions: 3 (last: failed — summary_failed, 5m ago)
🧹 Compactions: 4 (last: compacted just now)
```

Sessions without the new fields render exactly as before. The three skip-class buckets were consolidated into a shared `isCompactionSkipClassification` helper (previously duplicated in two files, now needed by a third call site). Observer-only: no compaction behavior changes, no new config surface, no schema migration (optional fields on the existing store entry, reserved in `session-entry-slot-keys` per its compile-time guard).

## User Impact

Operators can diagnose compaction problems after the fact from `/status` instead of having to reproduce them while watching logs. "Context keeps overflowing" support cases become answerable with one command: the status line now distinguishes "compaction is failing (`summary_failed`)" from "compaction keeps being skipped (`below_threshold`)" from "compaction works fine". Sessions that predate the change show the unchanged bare counter.

## Evidence

HEAD: `0797012ddbc598b9d63b2512e0c80a0162c64267` (rebased onto upstream/main `8d535fb039`; clean rebase, patch content unchanged)

Real behavior proof (no mocks — production `recordCompactionOutcome`/`incrementCompactionCount` persisting through the real session-store patch path to an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` file, rendered by the production `buildStatusMessage`; captured 2026-07-03 at this HEAD):

```
=== BEFORE (no outcome tracked yet) ===
📚 Context: ?/200k · 🧹 Compactions: 2

=== ACTION 1: production recordCompactionOutcome(failed, summary_failed) ===
persisted entry fields: {
  compactionCount: 2,
  lastCompactionAt: 1783047156063,
  lastCompactionOutcome: 'failed',
  lastCompactionReason: 'summary_failed',
  updatedAt: 1783047155879
}
📚 Context: ?/200k · 🧹 Compactions: 2 (last: failed — summary_failed, just now)

=== ACTION 2: production incrementCompactionCount (successful compaction) ===
persisted entry fields: {
  compactionCount: 3,
  lastCompactionAt: 1783047156077,
  lastCompactionOutcome: 'compacted',
  lastCompactionReason: undefined
}
📚 Context: ?/200k · 🧹 Compactions: 3 (last: compacted just now)
```

(`updatedAt` 1783047155879 predates the failed-stamp `lastCompactionAt` 1783047156063 — the failed attempt did not count as session activity.)

Focused tests (all green locally at this HEAD):

- `src/auto-reply/reply/session-updates.test.ts` — 7 (6 new: success stamp + stale-reason clear, zero-amount no-stamp, failed/skipped record without `updatedAt` churn, deleted-row no-resurrection on disk and in memory, delayed-older-attempt no-overwrite, unknown-session no-op)
- `src/status/status-message.test.ts` — 5 (3 new: failed render with bucket, compacted render, legacy bare counter)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.test.ts` — 12 (skip outcome recorded with `below_threshold`, failed outcome recorded with `summary_failed`)
- `src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts` — transcript-trim compaction stamps outcome (extended existing trim test)
- `src/agents/command/session-store.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.compaction.test.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compact-reasons.test.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory*.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server.sessions.compaction.test.ts` — all green
- `pnpm tsgo:core` + `pnpm tsgo:core:test` clean; changed-scope test fanout green (`OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1`, capped workers; the default-worker run on this host hit vitest worker OOM, an environment limit, not a diff failure)
- External structured review: Codex (GPT-5.5) closeout loop, 7 rounds — 5 accepted findings fixed (deleted-row resurrection on disk / in memory, delayed out-of-order stamps, stale full-entry patch rollback, gateway trim-path coverage), final round clean: "patch is correct", no actionable findings

Known limits: auto-compaction failures that happen *inside* a live embedded run surface through the run's own failure path and are not stamped by this PR (only successful-count reconciliation exists at that seam today); the stamped seams cover manual `/compact`, gateway RPC compact (LLM + trim), preflight/budget compaction, and CLI compaction.

Non-scope: no compaction behavior/retry changes; no new config; no fix for #49380 ("Plugin context engines cannot increment /status compaction count" — a different ask about count accuracy for plugin-owned engines); `openclaw status` CLI (status-all) surface unchanged — this touches the chat `/status` renderer where the counter already lives.

---

🤖 AI-assisted (Claude Fable 5 + Codex GPT-5.5 review loop). Prompts: translate agentic-coding-tool observability patterns (Claude Code changelog: compaction outcome visibility) into a narrow OpenClaw `/status` improvement; implementation, tests, structured review rounds, and the real-behavior proof were run locally as described above.

target.title: feat(release): add monthly npm stable publication
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot currently publish a trailing-month core package to the npm `stable` dist-tag without either treating it like a regular `latest` release or adopting the much larger superseded release-policy framework. The existing Full Release Validation graph also rejects the required `stable/YYYY.M.33` workflow ref, making a guarded monthly stable run unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one npm-only stable mode to the existing release workflow. Final `YYYY.M.PATCH` versions at patch `33` or later must publish from the exact `stable/YYYY.M.33` branch, with the release tag, checkout, branch tip, package version, preflight run, Full Release Validation run, manifest, and promoted tarball all bound to the same commit.

The implementation reuses the existing preflight manifest v1 and tested tarball, captures the prior npm `stable` selector before mutation, performs bounded exact-version and selector readback, and records a selector-only repair command. Full Release Validation now narrowly trusts the canonical stable branch shape and verifies every required child run used the target SHA. Plugin publication, native platforms, GitHub Releases, private dist-tags, Docker, mobile, and website publication remain out of scope.

Protected `main` must be on any strictly later calendar month with a daily patch below `33`, so supported maintenance patches remain publishable after development advances more than one month.

Fork and non-production rehearsals can explicitly set `bypass_stable_guard=true` to relax the `.33` threshold and protected-`main` month policy. The bypass is stable-only and default-off; it still requires the canonical stable branch, branch-tip/tag/checkout SHA equality, final tag/package identity, authenticated validation evidence, the verified tarball, environment approval, and registry proof.

## User Impact

Release operators can publish the completed month's core `openclaw` package to npm `stable`, beginning at `.33`, without moving `latest` or invoking other publication surfaces. Maintainers can exercise the same guarded path with a historical test version by enabling the audited bypass. Existing user-facing `stable | beta | dev` CLI channel behavior is unchanged by this PR; the CLI/channel migration remains separate work.

## Evidence

- Focused Vitest: 6 files, 199 tests passed.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs`: passed, including zizmor and direct-input interpolation checks.
- Focused oxlint and formatting checks: passed.
- Core test TypeScript check: passed.
- `node --check scripts/openclaw-npm-stable-release.mjs`: passed.
- `bash -n scripts/openclaw-npm-publish.sh`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent code, dead-code, documentation, and Full Validation reachability reviews found no remaining blocker or major issue.

## Manual Validation

- Verified the real release-check trusted-ref shell guard accepts `stable/2026.6.33` and `stable/2026.12.33` while rejecting zero-padded, out-of-range, wrong-patch, suffixed, and arbitrary stable refs.
- Verified the workflow contract dispatches CI, plugin prerelease, release checks, and performance from the stable workflow ref with the resolved target SHA, and fails closed if a required child head SHA differs.
- Verified `bypass_stable_guard` is rejected for non-stable tags and malformed values, preserves canonical branch and release identity, and relaxes only patch/month eligibility.
- Live stable preflight, environment approval, npm publication, and registry readback are intentionally pending; this PR does not claim production publication proof.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has strong sessions, Gateway, tasks, subagents, and operator surfaces, but long-running multi-agent work still needs a small core contract for durable session/task runtime state: run identity, step identity, event ordering, child links, recovery markers, and read-only inspection.

This PR is the RFC/architecture decision point for that boundary. It replaces the older RFC discussion in #97507 with updated naming and scope:

- `durable_runtime_*` instead of workflow-oriented schema naming;
- runtime runs/steps/events/refs/signals/timers/links as the core primitives;
- local-first shared state DB posture;
- Task Flow, Workboard, Work module, and external PM tools as projections/follow-ups, not prerequisites;
- no product-specific terminology.

## Dependency Chain

This is PR1 in the replacement durable runtime stack:

1. PR1: RFC v2 docs only, this PR.
2. PR2: durable runtime foundation, schema/store/CLI/Gateway read-only inspection.
3. PR3: agent/session/subagent wiring on top of PR2.

PR2 and PR3 should be reviewed only after this boundary is acceptable.

Docs only. No runtime behavior changes.

Mattermost post validation source: https://github.com/mattermost/mattermost/blob/master/server/public/model/post.go

target.title: fix: inbound messages can be reprocessed after gateway restart or reconnect (persistent replay dedupe + bounded durable replay)
target.body:
Fixes #97538
Part of #69208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound messages could be **reprocessed after a gateway restart or channel reconnect**, producing duplicate agent runs and, in the worst case, an unrecoverable re-delivery storm:

- **Discord / LINE / Mattermost**: the inbound replay dedupe guard was memory-only, so any event the platform re-delivers across a restart (Discord gateway resume, LINE webhook retry, Mattermost websocket replay) was processed again as a fresh message. Sibling channels (Telegram, iMessage, Nextcloud Talk) already persist this guard.
- **WhatsApp (#97538, Bug 2)**: the durable inbound journal replayed *all* pending events on every reconnect with no attempt accounting, no cap, and no dead-letter (pending TTL: 30 days). A poison event — e.g. a heavy multimodal batch whose run stalls before `complete()` — re-delivered on every reconnect forever, and restarting the gateway (the intuitive remediation) re-triggered the storm.

#97538's **Bug 1** (`abort_embedded_run` with `released=0`, owner lock never freed) is the same defect as #91700 and was already fixed by #91802 (`f194be19e2`, shipped in v2026.6.10/v2026.6.11); the reporter was on v2026.6.5. With Bug 1 fixed, the remaining live defect on `main` was the unbounded replay this PR removes. Asks 3 (ingress drain/ack CLI verb) and 4 (replay age threshold) from #97538 are operator/product decisions left to maintainers.

## Why This Change Was Made

One theme: **inbound accept must be idempotent and bounded across restarts**, enforced at the existing chokepoints instead of per-channel patches.

- The three memory-only channels flip to the existing SDK persistent claimable dedupe (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`), exactly the shape Telegram/iMessage already use. TTLs and in-memory caps are preserved per channel.
- The durable inbound receive journal (C3 chokepoint, `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts`) gains its missing terminal state — `fail()` (queue-backed: proper `failed` tombstone via the ingress queue; store-backed: terminal tombstone) — and a canonical `replayPendingDurableInboundReceives({ journal, maxAttempts, process })` helper that counts each replay attempt *before* processing (so stalls and crashes still converge), skips records whose row vanished between the pending snapshot and the attempt (concurrent complete/prune → no stale double-delivery), isolates per-record processing errors (one poison record cannot starve the rest of the pass), and dead-letters at the cap. WhatsApp's inline replay loop is deleted in favor of the helper (`WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5`, a bound on total delivery attempts). No new config surface; the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue already had `attempts` and `fail()` — WhatsApp just never used them (Telegram's ingress spool already does).
- The three flipped guards wire `onDiskError` warning logs (persistent dedupe fails open on storage errors; without the hook a broken state DB silently downgrades to memory-only), matching the telegram/nextcloud-talk/raft precedent.
- Test infrastructure: persistent dedupe means suites that reuse fixed message ids need per-test state isolation (`--isolate=false` safety). A shared `installIsolatedPluginStateDirForTests` helper (SDK test runtime) replaces per-suite hand-rolled scaffolds and is applied to the five affected suites, including `message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` which was committing fixed ids through the real guard.

Non-goals: the ingress drain/ack operator verb and reconnect age-threshold policy (asks 3/4 of #97538), and the stale-claim startup sweep (#90989 covers that separately).

Overlap disclosure: open PR #86577 pursues the same intent for the Discord slice (persist the inbound replay guard) but via a file-backed state dir, which predates the plugin-state SQLite migration and conflicts with the current "SQLite only" storage policy; it has failing CI and is waiting on author. This PR covers that surface with the canonical SQLite plugin-state path (the same shape Telegram/iMessage use). If this lands, #86577 should be closed as superseded.

## User Impact

- Discord, LINE, and Mattermost users no longer receive duplicate agent replies when the platform re-delivers an inbound event across a gateway restart.
- WhatsApp deployments can no longer wedge into the #97538 restart-amplified re-delivery loop: a pending inbound event is replayed at most 5 times across reconnects, then dead-lettered with a warning log (`dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts`), keeping the lane healthy. Successfully processed events are unaffected (they complete as before and never replay).

## Evidence

- TDD: every fix landed RED→GREEN.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts`, `extensions/line/src/webhook-replay-persist.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`: a committed replay key on a fresh guard instance (= restart) now reports `duplicate` (fails on memory-only guards).
  - `src/channels/message/durable-receive.test.ts` (+6): `fail()` dead-letters on both journal flavors and blocks re-accept; bounded replay processes fresh records, records attempts across stalled replays (`attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter at cap), dead-letters poison events, isolates a throwing record while still replaying the rest, and skips a record whose row vanished before the attempt was recorded.
- Suites: WhatsApp **979/979**, Discord **1810/1810**, LINE **292/292**, `src/channels/message/` **171/171**, `src/plugin-state/` **34/34**; mattermost green except `client.retry.test.ts`, which fails identically on the branch base `6cb82eaab8` (pre-existing, unrelated HTTP-retry suite).
- `pnpm build` clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK (baseline regenerated for the new exports); oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- An 8-angle multi-agent self-review ran on the branch; accepted findings (release-return guard, poison-record isolation, `onDiskError` logging, test state-dir isolation, SDK-surface trims, API baseline) are fixed in the final commit.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` ran locally (per CONTRIBUTING); its single P2 finding — adding a required `fail` method to the shipped `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` SDK type would break external implementers — is addressed: the shipped type is untouched and both factories now return a `DurableInboundReceiveReplayableJournal` intersection that carries `fail`.
- Import-boundary inventories clean (`check-src-extension-import-boundary`, `check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary` both `[]`); `pnpm test:contracts` 955 passed with 2 failures under triage as pre-existing (evidence below if confirmed).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure noted for reviewers: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.test.ts` (2 tests, native streaming usage compat) fails standalone with impl+test byte-identical to base `6cb82eaab8`.
- Known follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: persistent-dedupe per-message SQLite write cost is the same as the existing telegram/imessage guards (amortizing the eviction sweep is a separate perf change); the journal facade's prune-per-release/complete transaction amplification predates this PR; `createClaimableDedupe` defaults `stateMaxEntries` to 1 when omitted (all callers here pass it explicitly).

**Real gateway restart-replay proof** (details + logs in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365#issuecomment-4872867728)): on a real local gateway built from this branch (isolated `$HOME`, LINE channel, signed webhooks), event `m-proof-1` was delivered and processed, the gateway process was killed and restarted, and the platform-style redelivery of the same event was **deduped across the restart** (`line: skipped replayed webhook event message:m-proof-1`) while a fresh event was processed normally; both replay keys are visible in `plugin_state_entries` (`line.webhook-replay.*`). Discord/Mattermost flip the identical mechanism.

**Why the WhatsApp half has no live repro.** The #97538 failure state cannot be reproduced on demand: the reporter's pending backlog accumulated over ~7 days of production WhatsApp traffic, and ClawSweeper's 2026-06-28 review of the issue likewise states no high-confidence live current-main reproduction exists. That half is validated at the exact layer where the defect lives:

- The queue-backed journal tests run against the **real SQLite `channel_ingress_events` queue** (temp state dir), not mocks — `fail()` tombstones, attempt counting, and dead-letter-at-cap are exercised on the production storage engine.
- The "stall" mode that drives the storm is simulated directly: a replay pass whose `process` neither completes nor releases (the exact signature of a wedged run) must still record the attempt — asserted as `attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter across passes.
- The restart boundary is what the persistence tests simulate by construction: a **fresh guard/journal instance against the same persisted namespace** is semantically identical to a process restart (empty in-memory state, same durable rows). A live restart exercises no additional code path in the changed surface.
- The channel-side wiring is a thin adapter (constants + logging callback) covered by the full WhatsApp suite (986 tests), and the healthy path is behaviorally unchanged: completed events never replay (as before), and the cap only engages after 5 failed attempts of the same event.

#97538 Bug 1 provenance for reviewers: `f194be19e2` ("fix(diagnostics): release wedged session lane when stuck recovery aborts with queued session work", #91802, fixes #91700) is contained in v2026.6.10+ (`gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/compare/v2026.6.10...f194be19e2` → `behind`).

target.title: fix: chat.send no reply when thinking metadata is set
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a normal `chat.send` message with per-message `thinking` metadata could persist the user turn but produce no assistant response. The gateway was converting structured `thinking` metadata into textual `/think ...` command input, so clients without text slash-command authority could have a normal message treated as command text before model dispatch.

No related open GitHub issue or PR was found. I searched live GitHub and local gitcrawl for `chat.send thinking`, Android/chat no-reply reports, `/think` command-body reports, and paired-device slash-command authorization reports. The only direct keyword hit was already-merged #79385, which is a broader thinking/fast controls PR rather than this no-reply bug report.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.send` already has a structured dispatch path for one-turn thinking metadata via `replyOptions.thinkingLevelOverride`. This PR removes the duplicate `/think <level> <message>` rewrite for normal messages, leaving `CommandBody`, `BodyForCommands`, and `CommandTurn.body` as the user’s actual message while still passing the requested thinking override to reply resolution.

The review pass also hardened the adjacent reply/model-selection behavior so explicit thinking-off inputs, per-agent thinking defaults, and per-model `params.thinking` defaults prevent model reasoning defaults from being re-enabled during normal directive resolution and auto-fallback primary probes.

## User Impact

Mobile, WebChat, consult, and other `chat.send` clients can set a one-shot thinking level without accidentally turning a normal user message into a text slash command. `thinking` remains turn-local metadata: it applies to the dispatched run, does not alter the visible/user command text, and does not persist `thinkingLevel` into the session store.

## Evidence

Behavioral proof:

- `chat.send` with `message: "hello from phone"` and `thinking: "low"` now dispatches with `BodyForCommands === "hello from phone"`, `CommandBody === "hello from phone"`, `CommandTurn.kind === "normal"`, and `replyOptions.thinkingLevelOverride === "low"`.
- The persisted session store is checked at the canonical `agent:main:main` key and the legacy `main` view to prove one-turn `thinking` metadata does not become durable session `thinkingLevel`.
- Auto-fallback tests cover `params.thinking` values `false`, `"disabled"`, and `"none"` so configured thinking-off aliases keep reasoning defaults off when probing a primary model.

- What did NOT change:

target.title: fix(migrations): archive legacy config-health.json when all entries tracked in SQLite
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`config-health.json` legacy-state migration warning fires on **every** `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway restart`, and `openclaw doctor` invocation, and can never be resolved.

Root cause: `migrateLegacyConfigHealth()` compares legacy JSON entries against SQLite using `JSON.stringify` of the full fingerprint (including `observedAt` timestamps). The live config-health system independently writes updated fingerprints to SQLite, so the comparison always differs. The code sets `shouldArchive = conflictCount === 0`, meaning a single timestamp difference blocks archiving forever.

Fix: change the archive condition to `conflictCount === 0 || entriesToInsert.length === 0`. When all legacy entries already have corresponding SQLite rows (even with timestamp drift), there is nothing left to migrate and the file can be safely archived.

## Evidence

**Before-fix test (added regression test):** A test that pre-populates SQLite with a config-health row that has a different `observedAt` timestamp than the legacy JSON file. Without the fix, the migration reports a conflict and refuses to archive the file, causing the warning to persist across every CLI invocation.

**After-fix test:** The same test now archives the file successfully. The warning message is updated to reflect that the entries are already tracked in SQLite.

All 39 state-migrations tests pass:
```
 ✓ |infra| state-migrations.test.ts > state migrations > migrates legacy config health JSON into shared SQLite state
 ✓ |infra| state-migrations.test.ts > state migrations > archives legacy config health JSON when all entries already exist in SQLite (even with timestamp drift)
```

## Merge Risk

Low. This only changes the archive condition for a one-way legacy migration. The change is: when all config_paths from the legacy file already have rows in SQLite, archive the file instead of leaving it in place forever. No data is lost — it's already in SQLite.

Fixes #99280
Closes #99057 (incidental)

target.title: fix(agent-runner): classify transient provider errors as fallback-worthy
target.body:
## Summary

When a primary provider returns an `upstream_error` / `HTTP 500` / transient server error, the embedded agent run result classifier discards it (returns null), so `runWithModelFallback` never advances to the next configured fallback model. The turn ends immediately with `LLM request failed` even when healthy fallback models are configured and ready.

Fixes #95519

## Changes

- **`result-fallback-classifier.ts`**: Renamed `classifyBusinessDenialErrorPayloadReason` → `classifyProviderErrorPayloadReason` and extended the switch statement to also pass through `server_error` and `timeout` failover reasons (previously only `auth`/`auth_permanent`/`billing` were passed through).
- **`result-fallback-classifier.test.ts`**: Updated the "does not retry non-business transport error payloads" test case to expect a proper fallback classification for `HTTP 500: internal server error` instead of null.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Provider transient errors (`upstream_error`, `HTTP 500`, server timeout) now correctly trigger configured model fallbacks instead of ending the turn immediately.

**Evidence type**: terminal

**Real setup tested**: Node v24.13.1, Linux x86_64, worktree branch on openclaw/openclaw@main

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/result-fallback-classifier.test.ts
node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/outcome-fallback-runtime-contract.test.ts
node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```
$ CI=true pnpm test -- src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/result-fallback-classifier.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)

$ CI=true pnpm test -- src/agents/outcome-fallback-runtime-contract.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)

$ CI=true pnpm test -- src/agents/model-fallback.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  82 passed (82)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 103 tests pass across 3 related test suites. The classifier now correctly identifies `server_error` and `timeout` provider errors as fallback-worthy alongside the existing `auth`/`auth_permanent`/`billing` classifications.

**What was not tested**: Live end-to-end verification with a real provider returning `upstream_error` was not performed. The fix is validated at the unit-test layer which directly covers the classification code path.

## Tests and validation

| Test Type | Result | Details |
|-----------|--------|---------|
| result-fallback-classifier | ✅ | 11/11 passed |
| outcome-fallback-runtime-contract | ✅ | 10/10 passed |
| model-fallback | ✅ | 82/82 passed |

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**Yes** — users with configured fallback models will now see automatic fallback on transient provider errors (`upstream_error`, `HTTP 500`, timeouts) instead of immediate turn failure. This is the intended fix.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**No**

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes` / `No`)

**No** — only the internal fallback classification path is changed; auth/auth_permanent errors already triggered fallback before this change.

What is the highest-risk area?
- Over-fallbacking if the classifier is too broad

How is that risk mitigated?
- Only `server_error` and `timeout` (two specific transient errors already identified by the existing `classifyFailoverReason` function) are added. All other classifications (format, rate_limit, overloaded, model_not_found, etc.) remain filtered out as before. The non-GPT model fallthrough path is unchanged.

What is the next action?
- Maintainer review

target.title: fix: inbound messages can be reprocessed after gateway restart or reconnect (persistent replay dedupe + bounded durable replay)
target.body:
Fixes #97538
Part of #69208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inbound messages could be **reprocessed after a gateway restart or channel reconnect**, producing duplicate agent runs and, in the worst case, an unrecoverable re-delivery storm:

- **Discord / LINE / Mattermost**: the inbound replay dedupe guard was memory-only, so any event the platform re-delivers across a restart (Discord gateway resume, LINE webhook retry, Mattermost websocket replay) was processed again as a fresh message. Sibling channels (Telegram, iMessage, Nextcloud Talk) already persist this guard.
- **WhatsApp (#97538, Bug 2)**: the durable inbound journal replayed *all* pending events on every reconnect with no attempt accounting, no cap, and no dead-letter (pending TTL: 30 days). A poison event — e.g. a heavy multimodal batch whose run stalls before `complete()` — re-delivered on every reconnect forever, and restarting the gateway (the intuitive remediation) re-triggered the storm.

#97538's **Bug 1** (`abort_embedded_run` with `released=0`, owner lock never freed) is the same defect as #91700 and was already fixed by #91802 (`f194be19e2`, shipped in v2026.6.10/v2026.6.11); the reporter was on v2026.6.5. With Bug 1 fixed, the remaining live defect on `main` was the unbounded replay this PR removes. Asks 3 (ingress drain/ack CLI verb) and 4 (replay age threshold) from #97538 are operator/product decisions left to maintainers.

## Why This Change Was Made

One theme: **inbound accept must be idempotent and bounded across restarts**, enforced at the existing chokepoints instead of per-channel patches.

- The three memory-only channels flip to the existing SDK persistent claimable dedupe (`createClaimableDedupe` with `pluginId`/`namespacePrefix`), exactly the shape Telegram/iMessage already use. TTLs and in-memory caps are preserved per channel.
- The durable inbound receive journal (C3 chokepoint, `src/channels/message/durable-receive.ts`) gains its missing terminal state — `fail()` (queue-backed: proper `failed` tombstone via the ingress queue; store-backed: terminal tombstone) — and a canonical `replayPendingDurableInboundReceives({ journal, maxAttempts, process })` helper that counts each replay attempt *before* processing (so stalls and crashes still converge), skips records whose row vanished between the pending snapshot and the attempt (concurrent complete/prune → no stale double-delivery), isolates per-record processing errors (one poison record cannot starve the rest of the pass), and dead-letters at the cap. WhatsApp's inline replay loop is deleted in favor of the helper (`WHATSAPP_DURABLE_INBOUND_MAX_REPLAY_ATTEMPTS = 5`, a bound on total delivery attempts). No new config surface; the shared `channel_ingress_events` queue already had `attempts` and `fail()` — WhatsApp just never used them (Telegram's ingress spool already does).
- The three flipped guards wire `onDiskError` warning logs (persistent dedupe fails open on storage errors; without the hook a broken state DB silently downgrades to memory-only), matching the telegram/nextcloud-talk/raft precedent.
- Test infrastructure: persistent dedupe means suites that reuse fixed message ids need per-test state isolation (`--isolate=false` safety). A shared `installIsolatedPluginStateDirForTests` helper (SDK test runtime) replaces per-suite hand-rolled scaffolds and is applied to the five affected suites, including `message-handler.bot-self-filter.test.ts` which was committing fixed ids through the real guard.

Non-goals: the ingress drain/ack operator verb and reconnect age-threshold policy (asks 3/4 of #97538), and the stale-claim startup sweep (#90989 covers that separately).

Overlap disclosure: open PR #86577 pursues the same intent for the Discord slice (persist the inbound replay guard) but via a file-backed state dir, which predates the plugin-state SQLite migration and conflicts with the current "SQLite only" storage policy; it has failing CI and is waiting on author. This PR covers that surface with the canonical SQLite plugin-state path (the same shape Telegram/iMessage use). If this lands, #86577 should be closed as superseded.

## User Impact

- Discord, LINE, and Mattermost users no longer receive duplicate agent replies when the platform re-delivers an inbound event across a gateway restart.
- WhatsApp deployments can no longer wedge into the #97538 restart-amplified re-delivery loop: a pending inbound event is replayed at most 5 times across reconnects, then dead-lettered with a warning log (`dropping durable WhatsApp inbound after max replay attempts`), keeping the lane healthy. Successfully processed events are unaffected (they complete as before and never replay).

## Evidence

- TDD: every fix landed RED→GREEN.
  - `extensions/discord/src/monitor/inbound-dedupe.test.ts`, `extensions/line/src/webhook-replay-persist.test.ts`, `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/inbound-replay-persist.test.ts`: a committed replay key on a fresh guard instance (= restart) now reports `duplicate` (fails on memory-only guards).
  - `src/channels/message/durable-receive.test.ts` (+6): `fail()` dead-letters on both journal flavors and blocks re-accept; bounded replay processes fresh records, records attempts across stalled replays (`attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter at cap), dead-letters poison events, isolates a throwing record while still replaying the rest, and skips a record whose row vanished before the attempt was recorded.
- Suites: WhatsApp **979/979**, Discord **1810/1810**, LINE **292/292**, `src/channels/message/` **171/171**, `src/plugin-state/` **34/34**; mattermost green except `client.retry.test.ts`, which fails identically on the branch base `6cb82eaab8` (pre-existing, unrelated HTTP-retry suite).
- `pnpm build` clean; `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `plugin-sdk:api:check` OK (baseline regenerated for the new exports); oxfmt/oxlint clean.
- An 8-angle multi-agent self-review ran on the branch; accepted findings (release-return guard, poison-record isolation, `onDiskError` logging, test state-dir isolation, SDK-surface trims, API baseline) are fixed in the final commit.
- `codex review --base upstream/main` ran locally (per CONTRIBUTING); its single P2 finding — adding a required `fail` method to the shipped `DurableInboundReceiveJournal` SDK type would break external implementers — is addressed: the shipped type is untouched and both factories now return a `DurableInboundReceiveReplayableJournal` intersection that carries `fail`.
- Import-boundary inventories clean (`check-src-extension-import-boundary`, `check-sdk-package-extension-import-boundary` both `[]`); `pnpm test:contracts` 955 passed with 2 failures under triage as pre-existing (evidence below if confirmed).
- Pre-existing, unrelated failure noted for reviewers: `src/plugin-sdk/provider-catalog-shared.test.ts` (2 tests, native streaming usage compat) fails standalone with impl+test byte-identical to base `6cb82eaab8`.
- Known follow-ups deliberately not in this PR: persistent-dedupe per-message SQLite write cost is the same as the existing telegram/imessage guards (amortizing the eviction sweep is a separate perf change); the journal facade's prune-per-release/complete transaction amplification predates this PR; `createClaimableDedupe` defaults `stateMaxEntries` to 1 when omitted (all callers here pass it explicitly).

**Real gateway restart-replay proof** (details + logs in [this comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99365#issuecomment-4872867728)): on a real local gateway built from this branch (isolated `$HOME`, LINE channel, signed webhooks), event `m-proof-1` was delivered and processed, the gateway process was killed and restarted, and the platform-style redelivery of the same event was **deduped across the restart** (`line: skipped replayed webhook event message:m-proof-1`) while a fresh event was processed normally; both replay keys are visible in `plugin_state_entries` (`line.webhook-replay.*`). Discord/Mattermost flip the identical mechanism.

**Why the WhatsApp half has no live repro.** The #97538 failure state cannot be reproduced on demand: the reporter's pending backlog accumulated over ~7 days of production WhatsApp traffic, and ClawSweeper's 2026-06-28 review of the issue likewise states no high-confidence live current-main reproduction exists. That half is validated at the exact layer where the defect lives:

- The queue-backed journal tests run against the **real SQLite `channel_ingress_events` queue** (temp state dir), not mocks — `fail()` tombstones, attempt counting, and dead-letter-at-cap are exercised on the production storage engine.
- The "stall" mode that drives the storm is simulated directly: a replay pass whose `process` neither completes nor releases (the exact signature of a wedged run) must still record the attempt — asserted as `attempts` 1 → 2 → dead-letter across passes.
- The restart boundary is what the persistence tests simulate by construction: a **fresh guard/journal instance against the same persisted namespace** is semantically identical to a process restart (empty in-memory state, same durable rows). A live restart exercises no additional code path in the changed surface.
- The channel-side wiring is a thin adapter (constants + logging callback) covered by the full WhatsApp suite (986 tests), and the healthy path is behaviorally unchanged: completed events never replay (as before), and the cap only engages after 5 failed attempts of the same event.

#97538 Bug 1 provenance for reviewers: `f194be19e2` ("fix(diagnostics): release wedged session lane when stuck recovery aborts with queued session work", #91802, fixes #91700) is contained in v2026.6.10+ (`gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/compare/v2026.6.10...f194be19e2` → `behind`).

target.title: fix(qqbot): add TCP keepalive + heartbeat interval logging to prevent silent connection drops
target.body:
### Problem

**Messages delayed by up to 9 minutes due to silent WebSocket connection failures.**

On 2026-05-04 07:13, a user sent a message via QQBot. The message was not received until 07:22:18 — **9 minutes of delay**. During this entire period, the OpenClaw gateway showed no errors, no reconnection attempts, and no heartbeat failures. The connection appeared healthy but was in fact dead.

**What actually happened:**
- The QQ WebSocket connection was open from 07:04:03 to 07:22:16 (18 minutes, no drops logged)
- At 07:22:16, the connection abruptly closed with code `1006` (abnormal close, no close frame)
- Immediately after reconnecting at 07:22:18, all queued messages arrived at once
- **Conclusion:** The connection silently died well before 07:13, but neither the client nor the QQ server detected it. Messages were buffered server-side and only delivered after the client reconnect.

**Why no detection?** The existing QQBot gateway implementation has two gaps:
1. **No TCP keepalive** — The `ws` library was instantiated without `setKeepAlive`, meaning the OS-level TCP connection is not probed. Network middleboxes (routers, NAT, firewalls) silently drop idle connections without sending RST/FIN.
2. **No heartbeat timeout detection** — If the server sends a `HEARTBEAT_ACK` on time, the client assumes the connection is healthy. But if the `HEARTBEAT_ACK` is lost in transit (because the underlying TCP path is dead), the client never notices. There is no timeout or ACK validation.

**Root cause:** The 1006 abnormal close indicates the connection was terminated without a proper WebSocket close frame — likely at the TCP or network layer (NAT timeout, silent packet drop). The client had no way to detect this before receiving a message, because there was no lower-level keepalive probe and no heartbeat ACK timeout.

### Solution

**Three changes in `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway-connection.ts`:**

#### 1. TCP Keepalive (Prevention)
```typescript
const socket = (ws as unknown as { _socket: Socket | null })._socket;
if (socket) {
  socket.setKeepAlive(true, 30_000);  // probe every 30s
  socket.setTimeout(60_000);          // 60s with no data → timeout
  socket.on("timeout", () => {
    log?.warn?.(`WebSocket socket timeout — closing and reconnecting`);
    ws.close();  // triggers existing reconnect flow
  });
}
```

- `setKeepAlive(true, 30_000)` — OS sends TCP keepalive probes every 30 seconds, keeping NAT mappings alive and detecting dead connections at the transport layer
- `setTimeout(60_000)` — if no data (including keepalive ACK) is received for 60 seconds, the socket is considered dead and closed, triggering an immediate reconnect

#### 2. Heartbeat Interval Logging (Debugging)
```typescript
const interval = d.heartbeat_interval;
this.ctx.log?.info(`Heartbeat interval: ${interval}ms (${(interval / 1000).toFixed(1)}s)`);
```

- Logs the heartbeat interval sent by the QQ server on every connect/resume
- Previously unknown: QQ server uses **41.25 seconds**, not a round number
- Critical for diagnosing heartbeat-related issues in the future

#### 3. WebSocket Compression
```typescript
perMessageDeflate: true
```
- Standard best practice for `ws` library; reduces bandwidth for JSON payloads

### Verification

- **7 new unit tests** for keepalive and heartbeat logging logic
- **50 existing tests** pass (message-queue, outbound-dispatch, inbound-pipeline, envelope-stage)
- **Live deployment test:** After deploying, TCP socket timeout was correctly detected on a dead connection at 10:38:48, triggering automatic reconnect. Heartbeat interval logged as `41250ms (41.3s)`.

### Expected Impact

- **Before:** Dead connections go undetected for minutes. Users see message delays of 5-10 minutes. Only a manual restart or the next server-side close triggers reconnect.
- **After:** Dead connections detected within 60 seconds via TCP keepalive timeout. Automatic reconnect restores message delivery. Heartbeat interval visible in logs for troubleshooting.

target.title: fix(cli): bound approvals file read size in exec-approvals-cli
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `--file` path in the approvals `set` command reads the target JSON file with an unbounded `await fs.readFile()`, so a user that accidentally passes a very large file (e.g., a multi-GB log instead of an approvals JSON) would cause Node to buffer the whole payload, allocating OOM memory. The `--stdin` path already has a 1 MB bound via `readStdin()`, but the `--file` path was missing the equivalent guard.

**Solution**: Add `readFileWithBound(filePath, maxBytes)` — an fd-based bounded read helper that opens the file, validates it via the same file descriptor (TOCTOU-safe), rejects non-regular files, and reads into a fixed-size buffer with a `maxBytes + 1` cap. Use it in place of the unbounded `fs.readFile()` for the approvals `set --file` path.

**What changed**:
- New `readFileWithBound()` function in `src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts`
- Approvals `set --file` handler now calls `readFileWithBound()` instead of `fs.readFile()`
- Added 3 test cases: valid small file, oversized file rejection, non-regular (directory) rejection
- Exported `readFileWithBound` via `testing` object for unit test access

**What did NOT change**:
- All existing behavior for valid small approvals JSON files — they continue to parse through `JSON5.parse` and `saveSnapshotTargeted`
- The `--stdin` path — it was already bounded and is unchanged
- CLI interface, output format, error messages for non-boundary cases
- No configuration changes, no dependency changes

## What Problem This Solves

The approvals CLI accepts a `--file` argument pointing to a JSON file. On the `set` action, the file content is read, parsed as JSON5, and written to the local approvals store. Previously, the file read used a bare `await fs.readFile(filePath, "utf8")` with no size limit, so a path pointing to a multi-GB file (e.g., a log or /dev/zero) would cause Node to allocate memory for the entire payload before any parsing could reject it.

This is defense-in-depth and sibling-consistency cleanup: the `--stdin` path was already bounded by `EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`, but the `--file` path was not.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Bound the approvals `--file` read to 1 MB max, rejecting oversized and non-regular files with a clear error message instead of allocating unbounded memory.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.1.0, local openclaw CLI dev build (pnpm openclaw).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Scenario 1: Normal small file succeeds
echo '{"version":1,"agents":{}}' > /tmp/test-approvals.json
pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp/test-approvals.json
```

```bash
# Scenario 2: Oversized file rejected
dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/huge-approvals.bin bs=1M count=2
pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp/huge-approvals.bin
```

```bash
# Scenario 3: Non-regular file (directory) rejected
pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
# Scenario 1 — Normal file succeeds
$ pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp/test-approvals.json
Writing local approvals.
Target: local
Approvals
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------+
| Field     | Value                                                      |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------+
| Target    | local                                                      |
| Path      | ~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json                            |
| Exists    | yes                                                        |
| Hash      | c5f4f89fe5158f7ffa01255d691f88ba629e3dad5cb05f8e8e...     |
| Version   | 1                                                          |
| Socket    | default                                                    |
| Defaults  | none                                                       |
| Agents    | 0                                                          |
| Allowlist | 0                                                          |
+-----------+------------------------------------------------------------+
No allowlist entries.

# Scenario 2 — Oversized file rejected
$ pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp/huge-approvals.bin
Writing local approvals.
Exec approvals file exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/huge-approvals.bin

# Scenario 3 — Directory path rejected
$ pnpm openclaw approvals set --file /tmp
Writing local approvals.
Exec approvals file is not a regular file: /tmp
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All three real-world scenarios behave correctly: (1) a 25-byte valid approvals JSON is accepted and written to the local store; (2) a 2 MB oversized file is cleanly rejected with a size-limit error before any read; (3) a directory path is rejected as "not a regular file" via stat.isFile(), preventing the /dev/zero-style bypass.

**What was not tested**: Named pipe (FIFO) without a writer — covered by unit test (rejects FIFO paths without blocking) but not manually verified with the CLI. Cross-platform behavior on macOS and Windows has not been tested (the O_NONBLOCK flag and stat.isFile() are POSIX primitives; Windows uses a different code path). External /dev/fd or /proc/self/fd paths that are regular-file symlinks but report size 0 are not explicitly enumerated — the stat check covers these via stat.size exceeding maxBytes when they have content, and the read-loop cap covers residual short-read cases. No load testing was performed on the bounded read loop — the scenario is an accidental large file, not sustained throughput.

## Evidence

Unit tests:

```
$ pnpm test src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Format (oxfmt):

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.ts src/cli/exec-approvals-cli.test.ts
  (clean)
```

## Risk checklist

**What is the highest-risk area in this change**: The new readFileWithBound opens the file with O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK and reads via the same fd — a TOCTOU-safe pattern. The highest risk is a FIFO (named pipe) without a writer on a platform where O_NONBLOCK is not supported (non-POSIX); the test validates this and the error path degrades to a readable error.

**Mitigation**: O_NONBLOCK fails fast on FIFO stalls and is already used elsewhere in the codebase (SCRIPT_PREFLIGHT_OPEN_FLAGS in bash-tools.exec.ts). The read loop caps consumption to maxBytes + 1 bytes and throws before any JSON parsing — OOM is structurally impossible regardless of the input.

**Risk level**: Low — the change is additive (adds a guard where none existed) and preserves all existing behavior for valid inputs. The bounded read matches the pattern of the already-merged readStdin().

**Merge-risk explanation**: availability — the PR fixes an unbounded-read availability issue. The implementation uses fd-based read (replacing the initial stat-only guard), which closes the TOCTOU and non-regular-file bypass paths identified in review.

**Label**: security

_AI-assisted._

target.title: fix(session-memory): use shortenHomePath for safe home-path display in logs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`saveSessionMemoryNow` in the session-memory hook uses `memoryFilePath.replace(os.homedir(), "~")` to shorten home paths in log output. When `HOME=/home/user`, a path like `/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md` is corrupted to `~2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md` — the sibling directory prefix `/home/user` is replaced indiscriminately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace ad hoc `String.replace()` with the existing boundary-aware `shortenHomePath()` utility that checks token boundaries before substituting. Same bug pattern as #98876 (home path replacement).

## User Impact

Session-memory hook log output now correctly shows sibling paths without corruption. Home-relative paths are still shortened to `~/...` as before.

## Evidence

### Committed test proof

The test verifies sibling path protection with real `shortenHomePath`:

```ts
it("preserves sibling paths that share a home prefix", async () => {
  vi.stubEnv("HOME", "/home/user");
  try {
    const { shortenHomePath } = await import("../../../utils.js");
    // Sibling path must not be corrupted
    expect(shortenHomePath("/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md"))
      .toBe("/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md");
    // Home-relative path must still be shortened
    expect(shortenHomePath("/home/user/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md"))
      .toBe("~/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md");
  } finally { vi.unstubAllEnvs(); }
});
```

### Real behavior proof

With `HOME=/home/user`, the handler's log calls produce:

```
log.debug: "Memory file path resolved"
  path: "/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/2026-07-03.md"  ← preserved (was ~2/... before)
  path: "~/.openclaw/state/memory/2026-07-03.md"            ← still shortened for home paths

log.info: "Session context saved to /home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/2026-07-03.md"  ← correct
```

### Full test suite — 30/30 passed

```
pnpm test src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts

 ✓ session-memory hook > skips non-command events
 ✓ session-memory hook > skips commands other than new
 ✓ session-memory hook > creates memory file with session content on /new command
 ... (all 29 core hook tests)
 ✓ shortenHomePath sibling protection > preserves sibling paths that share a home prefix

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

### What changed

- `handler.ts`: replaced 2 uses of `memoryFilePath.replace(os.homedir(), "~")` with `shortenHomePath(memoryFilePath)`
- `handler.test.ts`: added sibling path protection regression test

## Risk

Low. The same `shortenHomePath` utility is tested in `src/utils.test.ts` and used in browser Chrome MCP diagnostics (#99113). The change is a 1:1 swap of path-shortening helpers.

- **What changed:** `createReplyPrefixContext()` now pre-seeds the `ResponsePrefixContext` with model, provider, and thinkingLevel resolved from config defaults, so early-exit paths like abort have valid values for template interpolation.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary):** No changes to abort logic, dispatch flow, template resolution engine, or `formatAbortReplyText()`. The `onModelSelected()` callback still overwrites the defaults at runtime during normal replies.

target.title: fix(agents): verify delivery receipts before display
target.body:
## Summary

This fixes a user-visible trust bug in the agent reply pipeline: assistant text can no longer present a message delivery receipt as fact unless the current turn has matching evidence from a successful message tool send.

- Before: model text could say a message was accepted, queued, sent, or include a provider id even when no send result backed that claim.
- After: unsupported delivery receipt claims are replaced before visible delivery, while matching current-turn send evidence still allows the receipt through.
- Scope is intentionally message-delivery only. This PR does not add a generic plugin evidence API or claim support for tickets, payments, calendar events, email, or other side effects.
- Reviewer focus: detector scope, evidence matching, and the stream/block/final payload guard points.

[size/exempt: 23 files, +2272/-41 because the fix needs proof across streaming, block replies, chunked replies, retry/final payload delivery, and tool-result evidence paths. This is not a mechanical PR.]

## Linked context

Related review/proof discussion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94693#issuecomment-4746612520

Current base/head used for local validation:

- Base: `origin/main` at `061a3705dbe28ddd058afb298976f09d8857b43b`
- Head: `7a9090a8373217979bc8e863bb8e1f7fa71e6a70`

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: user-visible agent replies could claim message delivery status or provider receipt ids without matching current-turn delivery evidence.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on this branch, using the production `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` bridge with real runtime events and no Vitest assertion runner.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `timeout -k5s 120s node --import tsx` with an inline script that imports `./src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.js`, sends actual `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_end`, and assistant `text_end` events, then asserts unsupported and verified visible replies.
- Evidence after fix:

```text
[proof-94693] unsupported claim visible reply: {"text":"I cannot verify that this SMS was sent. I do not have matching current-turn delivery evidence, so please check the messaging provider history or use the verified send flow before reporting it as sent.","audioAsVoice":false,"replyToTag":true,"replyToCurrent":true}
[proof-94693] verified delivery evidence: [{"channel":"sms","toolName":"message","providerId":"SM_proof_redacted_1234","status":"queued","sender":"+15557654321","recipient":"+15551234567"}]
[proof-94693] verified claim visible reply: {"text":"I sent the SMS. Status: accepted/queued. Message ID: SM_proof_redacted_1234","audioAsVoice":false,"replyToTag":false,"replyToCurrent":false}
[proof-94693] All runtime assertions passed.
```

- Observed result after fix: the unsupported receipt text never reaches the visible block reply; the verified receipt reaches the visible reply only after matching `message` tool delivery evidence is recorded.
- What was not tested: no live production SMS/Twilio send, no real phone delivery, no full `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` run.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the proof uses the local runtime bridge and synthetic redacted delivery receipt data. It proves OpenClaw's visible reply guard and evidence matching behavior, not external carrier delivery.
- Before evidence: the original incident class was an accepted/queued SMS confirmation with a message id that was not present in local delivery history.

## Tests and validation

Focused commands run locally:

```text
timeout -k5s 240s node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.test.ts src/agents/message-delivery-receipt-claims.test.ts src/agents/message-delivery-receipt-guard.test.ts src/agents/message-delivery-receipts.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.emits-block-replies-text-end-does-not.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.errors.test.ts

timeout -k5s 120s ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files>
git diff --check
codex review --base origin/main
```

Validation result:

- Vitest focused suite passed: `4` unit-fast files / `101` tests and `3` agents files / `109` tests.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local `codex review --base origin/main` found no discrete regression after the final review fixes.
- Browser testing was not applicable: this changes backend agent runtime delivery paths and has no browser-rendered route or dev server surface.

Regression coverage added or updated:

- Tool evidence path: successful send, broadcast, private tool-send receipts, failed results, dry-runs, read/no-op actions.
- Visible delivery paths: partial streams, block replies, chunked block replies, phase-aware streams, final payload assembly, and retry evidence carryover.
- Claim parsing: incident-style receipt text, first-person receipts, recipient matching, negated non-delivery wording, quoted diagnostics, explanatory field text, and non-SMS wording.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes`

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `No`

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `Yes`, in the narrow sense that visible tool-result claims are now checked against recorded current-turn tool evidence.

Highest-risk area: false positives in receipt detection could replace legitimate explanatory text.

Mitigation: the detector is intentionally limited to message/SMS-style receipt language, preserves explicit uncertainty and negated non-delivery statements, and has focused regression coverage for quoted diagnostics and explanatory field names.

## Current review state

Next action: maintainer and bot review on the narrowed message-delivery guard.

target.title: security: gateway public network hardening
target.body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive security hardening for OpenClaw Gateway when exposed to public networks (e.g. `https://openclaw.allegro.earth/`). The existing security mechanisms (non-loopback auth enforcement, auth rate limiting, CORS checks) leave gaps that this PR addresses:

- **IP access control** (allowlist/blocklist with CIDR support) — enforced on both HTTP requests and WebSocket upgrades, loopback always allowed, blocklist takes priority
- **Password/token strength validation** — CRITICAL startup warnings when network-exposed with short tokens (<32 chars) or weak passwords (<12 chars, all-digit/all-letter patterns)
- **TLS enforcement check** — CRITICAL startup warning when network-exposed without TLS and no `terminatedUpstream` declaration
- **Per-IP request rate limiting** — sliding window (default 120 req/min/IP), loopback exempt by default, returns 429 with Retry-After
- **Auth audit logging** — JSONL to `~/.openclaw/logs/gateway-auth.jsonl` with file rotation, records `auth_failure`, `auth_success`, `rate_limited`, `ip_blocked` events
- **Auto HSTS** — `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000` set automatically when TLS is enabled
- **Eliminate silent 0.0.0.0 fallback** — `loopback`, `tailnet`, and `custom` bind modes now throw clear errors instead of silently falling back to all-interfaces
- **New security audit checks** — `gateway.no_tls_network_exposed` (critical), `gateway.password_too_short` (critical), `gateway.password_weak_pattern` (warn), `gateway.no_request_rate_limit` (warn), `gateway.auto_bind_fallback` (warn)
- **Enhanced `doctor` warnings** — TLS, password strength, token length, request rate limit checks for network-exposed gateways

### Config additions (`gateway.*`)

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|-----|------|---------|-------------|
| `ipAllowlist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP allowlist (loopback always allowed) |
| `ipBlocklist` | `string[]` | — | CIDR/IP blocklist (checked before allowlist) |
| `requestRateLimit.maxRequests` | `number` | 120 | Max requests per IP per window |
| `requestRateLimit.windowMs` | `number` | 60000 | Sliding window duration (ms) |
| `requestRateLimit.exemptLoopback` | `boolean` | true | Skip rate limiting for localhost |
| `tls.terminatedUpstream` | `boolean` | false | Declare TLS terminated by reverse proxy |

## Test plan

target.title: Fix/hooks agent accountid normalization
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: `POST /hooks/agent` silently drops `accountId` from incoming payloads because `HookAgentPayload` lacks the field, `normalizeAgentPayload()` never extracts it, and `dispatchAgentHook()` hand-builds a `CronJob` bypassing `normalizeCronJobCreate()`.
- Why it matters: Multi-account WhatsApp (and any channel requiring `accountId`) delivery fails silently — the caller gets a success response but the message is never sent.
- What changed: Hook dispatch now routes through `normalizeCronJobCreate()`, which promotes legacy flat fields into proper `CronDelivery` with `accountId`. `resolveCronToolPolicy()` derives `disableMessageTool` for shared-contract callers from whether the target is fully resolved (explicit mode + accountId) instead of unconditionally disabling.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): The cron-owned path (`deliveryContract: "cron-owned"`) is untouched. No changes to `normalizeCronJobCreate()` logic itself — only a JSDoc addition. No new config options or API surface.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #43866
- Related #27015, #24186, #42244, #23853, #16925, #30052, #29090

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- `POST /hooks/agent` now correctly preserves `accountId` through to delivery, enabling multi-account WhatsApp delivery via hooks.
- For shared-contract hook runs with a fully resolved delivery target (explicit mode + accountId), the agent's message tool is no longer unconditionally disabled — it remains available as a fallback. The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) prevents duplicate sends.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? `No`
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? `No`
- New/changed network calls? `No`
- Command/tool execution surface changed? `No` — the message tool was already available for shared-contract callers without delivery; this change refines *when* it stays enabled based on target resolution quality.
- Data access scope changed? `No`

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: All (server-side code path)
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / Bun
- Model/provider: Any (not model/provider-specific)
- Integration/channel (if any): WhatsApp (any multi-account channel)
- Relevant config (redacted): Hooks enabled with token, WhatsApp channel configured with multiple `accountId` connections

### Steps

1. Configure two WhatsApp connections with distinct `accountId` values.
2. Send `POST /hooks/agent` with `{ "message": "Hello", "channel": "whatsapp", "to": "1234567890", "accountId": "botnumber" }`.
3. Observe delivery result.

### Expected

- `accountId` flows through to `CronDelivery.accountId`, `resolveDeliveryTarget()` identifies the correct WhatsApp connection, and the message is delivered.

### Actual (before fix)

- `accountId` is silently dropped. Delivery fails because no connection can be identified. Caller receives success response.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

New tests added in second commit:
- `src/gateway/hooks.test.ts` — `normalizeAgentPayload` extracts and trims `accountId` (present, absent, blank)
- `src/gateway/server.hooks.test.ts` — integration test: `accountId` propagates into `job.delivery` via cron normalization pipeline
- `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.message-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 tests for shared-contract tool policy: fully resolved target (explicit + accountId → enabled), missing accountId (→ disabled), implicitly resolved target (→ disabled)

Verification: `pnpm tsgo` clean, `pnpm check` clean, all 59 tests across the 4 test files pass.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: typecheck (`pnpm tsgo`), lint/format (`pnpm check`), unit + integration tests pass for all modified test files
- Edge cases checked: blank/missing `accountId`, `normalizeCronJobCreate` returning null (guard added), implicit vs explicit delivery target mode, `mode: "none"` (verified `deliveryRequested` is already `false` so no extra clause needed)
- What you did **not** verify: live end-to-end delivery through a real WhatsApp multi-account setup; only verified through unit/integration tests and code tracing

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? `Yes`
- Config/env changes? `No`
- Migration needed? `No`

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: Revert both commits; the hand-built CronJob path is fully self-contained in the reverted `dispatchAgentHook()`.
- Files/config to restore: `src/gateway/hooks.ts`, `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`, `src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`, `src/cron/normalize.ts`
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: Hook agent dispatches returning early with "normalizeCronJobCreate returned null" warning (would indicate the normalizer rejects a payload shape it previously accepted via hand-built path).

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: `normalizeCronJobCreate()` could reject a hook payload shape that the hand-built path previously accepted, causing hook dispatches to silently no-op.
  - Mitigation: A null-return guard logs a warning and still returns a `runId` to the caller. The normalizer is well-tested and accepts all fields the hook path provides. Integration test verifies the full pipeline.

- Risk: Enabling the message tool for shared-contract callers with fully resolved targets could cause duplicate sends (agent sends via tool + automatic delivery sends again).
  - Mitigation: The existing `skipMessagingToolDelivery` guard (`run.ts:821-831`) already detects when the agent's message tool sent to the same target and skips automatic delivery. This guard predates this change and is tested.

target.title: security: scan markdown skill definitions for injection threats
target.body:
## Summary

The skill scanner (`src/security/skill-scanner.ts`) previously only scanned JavaScript/TypeScript-style source files for threats. This PR extends it to also scan Markdown `.md` files, including `SKILL.md` definitions, for injection and obfuscation patterns.

Markdown-specific rules added:
- `hidden-unicode` detects zero-width characters and text-direction overrides that can hide malicious content from visual review.
- `markdown-data-uri` detects data URIs with executable MIME types such as `text/html` and `application/javascript`.
- `markdown-download-exec` detects `curl`/`wget` download-and-execute pipelines, including common bypass forms like `sudo bash`, `/bin/bash`, `python3`, line continuations, and quoted pipe characters inside arguments.
- `markdown-encoded-payload` detects large base64 blocks inside Markdown.
- `markdown-hex-payload` detects hex-encoded payloads inside Markdown.

Implementation notes:
- Added `MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS` and `isMarkdown()`.
- Added `.md` to `SCANNABLE_EXTENSIONS`.
- Applies Markdown-specific rules only to Markdown files, while preserving code-specific scanning behavior for code files.
- Uses the raw Markdown source for Markdown source-wide rules so URLs like `https://...` are not accidentally truncated by code-comment stripping.
- Adds focused tests for Markdown findings, Markdown/code rule separation, directory scanning, and summary counts.

Why this matters: skill definitions can include rendered Markdown. Without scanning these files, hidden instructions, obfuscated payloads, or download-and-execute commands in skill Markdown can bypass the existing code scanner.

Supersedes #10705 (auto-closed by stale bot). Rebased cleanly onto current `main`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 CHANGELOG.md src/security/skill-scanner.ts src/security/skill-scanner.test.ts`
- [x] `pnpm check:changed`

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Markdown skill definitions such as `SKILL.md` are now scanned for hidden Unicode, executable data URIs, download-and-execute pipelines, and encoded payloads that previously fell outside the JavaScript/TypeScript scanner surface.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS at `/Users/alexalaniz/Code/openclaw-43469`, based on current `openclaw/openclaw:main` (`24bd0b212f`), with dependencies installed using `pnpm@10.33.2`.
