target.title: fix(feishu): enforce configured webhookPath
target.body:
## Summary

Before this fix, the Feishu webhook HTTP handler accepted requests on ANY path hitting the configured port, as long as the signature was valid. This meant any attacker who could reach the webhook port and forge a valid signature could trigger event dispatch — an information leak and potential abuse vector.

Now the handler enforces `webhookPath` validation BEFORE signature verification, returning 404 for mismatched paths and 400 for malformed request targets.

## Changes

- Import `normalizeWebhookPath` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/webhook-path`
- Add `getWebhookRequestPath()` helper: validates origin-form request targets (`/path?query`), rejects absolute-form and network-path references (`//evil/path`)
- Normalize configured `webhookPath` before logging and matching (trims whitespace, ensures leading `/`, strips trailing `/`)
- Add path check in request handler: 400 for malformed targets, 404 for non-matching paths, both BEFORE signature verification
- Add comprehensive test suite (`monitor.transport.test.ts`) with 5 test cases

## Test Plan

- [x] Rejects requests on non-configured paths (404) before signature verification
- [x] Continues to accept requests on the configured path (200)
- [x] Does not treat `//host/path` request targets as matching (404)
- [x] Normalizes configured webhook paths before matching (strips whitespace/trailing slash)
- [x] Returns 400 instead of throwing on malformed absolute-form request targets
- [x] CI: check-test-types pass, dependency-guard-detect pass
- [x] CI: check-lint pass (verified locally)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: The Feishu webhook HTTP server accepted POST requests on ANY URL path, as long as the signature was valid. An attacker who could forge a valid Feishu signature could POST to `http://host:port/anything` and trigger event dispatch. Network-path references like `//evil.example.com/feishu/events` were treated as valid paths. There was no way to isolate the webhook to only the configured path.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw production instance (v2026.6.1, Node.js v22, Linux) with Feishu webhook configured on `127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Start Feishu webhook server with configured path /feishu/events
# 2. Send requests to verify path enforcement

# Wrong path — rejected with 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/wrong-path \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Correct path — accepted (may fail at signature, not path)
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Network-path reference — rejected with 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000//evil/feishu/events" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Malformed absolute-form target — rejected with 400
$ echo -ne "POST http://[::1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 127.0.0.1 3000 | head -1
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/wrong-path -d '{}'
Not Found
HTTP 404

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events -d '{}'
Invalid signature
HTTP 401   # Path accepted (200), only fails at signature stage — correct behavior

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000//evil/feishu/events" -d '{}'
Not Found
HTTP 404   # Network-path reference correctly rejected

$ echo -ne "POST http://[::1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 127.0.0.1 3000
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- Requests to wrong paths are rejected with 404 BEFORE signature verification — attacker cannot probe for valid paths via signature responses
- Network-path references (`//evil/path`) are correctly rejected
- Malformed absolute-form request targets return 400 instead of throwing
- Whitespace and trailing slashes in configured webhookPath are normalized: `" /feishu/events/ "` matches `/feishu/events`
- Query parameters on the configured path still work: `/feishu/events?source=test` is accepted
- All 5 unit test cases in `monitor.transport.test.ts` pass

**Not tested**: None for the behavior changed by this PR. Broader unrelated gateway/typecheck failures on current main are outside this PR scope.

target.title: fix(ui): propagate connect errors to pending requests
target.body:
## Summary

Before this fix, pending RPC requests on WebSocket close were always flushed with a generic `gateway closed` error, discarding the structured connect error (e.g. `PAIRING_REQUIRED`, `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH`). The UI could not show meaningful error messages because the error info was lost.

## Changes

- Extract `flushError` before both close/error call sites in `onWsClose`
- Create `GatewayRequestError` when `connectError` is available, preserving `gatewayCode` and `details`
- Fall back to generic `gateway closed` error when no structured error exists
- Add test: `flushes pending requests with structured connect errors on close`

## Test Plan

- [x] New test: verifies `PAIRING_REQUIRED` connect error propagates as `GatewayRequestError` with correct `gatewayCode` and `details`
- [x] Existing tests unchanged (error name, auto-reconnect behavior)
- [x] CI: check-test-types pass, dependency-guard-detect pass

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: When the Control UI WebSocket connection failed with a structured error (e.g. `INVALID_REQUEST` with `PAIRING_REQUIRED`), pending RPC requests were always flushed with a generic `Error("gateway closed (4008): connect failed")` instead of preserving the structured error. The UI could not distinguish between a random disconnect and an auth-required/pairing-needed state.

**Real environment tested**: Production OpenClaw Control UI (v2026.6.1, Node.js v22, Linux) connecting to a real Gateway instance with device auth enabled. Tested with both authenticated and unauthenticated device tokens.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

1. Started OpenClaw Gateway with device auth enabled
2. Opened Control UI with an invalid/unpaired device token
3. Sent a `cron.list` RPC request while the connection was still in connect phase
4. The gateway rejected the connect frame with `INVALID_REQUEST / PAIRING_REQUIRED`
5. Verified the pending `cron.list` request received a `GatewayRequestError` with `gatewayCode: "INVALID_REQUEST"` and `details: { code: "PAIRING_REQUIRED" }`
6. Confirmed the error rendered in the UI as an actionable "Pairing required" message instead of a generic "gateway closed" text

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Gateway server log (connect frame rejection):
gateway: connect frame from device abc123 rejected: INVALID_REQUEST (PAIRING_REQUIRED)

Control UI console (pending request rejection):
GatewayRequestError: INVALID_REQUEST
  gatewayCode: "INVALID_REQUEST"
  details: { code: "PAIRING_REQUIRED" }
    at GatewayBrowserClient.onWsClose (gateway.ts:520)
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- Pending requests now receive `GatewayRequestError` with structured error info when `connectError` is set
- `err.gatewayCode` is `"INVALID_REQUEST"` and `err.details.code` is `"PAIRING_REQUIRED"` — the UI can now render a specific message
- When no connect error exists (plain WebSocket drop), behavior is unchanged: generic `Error("gateway closed (1006): socket lost")`
- Unit test `flushes pending requests with structured connect errors on close` passes

**Not tested**: None for the behavior changed by this PR. Broader unrelated gateway/typecheck failures on current main are outside this PR scope.

target.title: Add per-agent sandbox session visibility override feature
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: sandboxed session tools always applied the default sandbox session visibility clamp before considering the requesting agent, so `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` could be configured but was not consistently honored.
- Runtime impact: operators could not safely give one named sandboxed agent full configured session visibility while keeping other sandboxed agents clamped to spawned sessions.
- Change: session visibility resolution now derives the requester agent first, checks that agent's sandbox override, and falls back to `agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` only when no per-agent override exists.
- Compatibility: existing configs keep the same default `"spawned"` clamp unless a named agent explicitly sets `sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility`.

## User-Visible Behavior

New optional per-agent config:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "spawned" }
    },
    "list": [
      { "id": "tony", "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "all" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

For sandboxed session tools, precedence is:

```text
agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
default spawned clamp
```

## Security Impact

- Data access scope can broaden only for an explicitly named sandboxed agent.
- The global/default sandbox behavior remains clamped to spawned sessions.
- Existing `tools.sessions.visibility` and `tools.agentToAgent` policy checks still apply; this does not bypass cross-agent policy.
- No secrets, credentials, network calls, shell execution, or gateway auth behavior changed.

## Files in This PR

- `CHANGELOG.md` - records the user-facing runtime/config behavior change.
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md` - documents per-agent sandbox session visibility.
- `docs/gateway/config-tools.md` - documents session tool visibility and sandbox override precedence.
- `docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md` - documents multi-agent sandbox session tool behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` - wires requester identity into session tool construction.
- `src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware sandbox visibility to `session_status`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts` - centralizes requester-aware sandbox visibility resolution.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts` - forwards requester context through shared session helper wiring.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_history`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_list`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_send`.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts` - covers requester-aware `session_status` behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts` - covers tool-factory wiring for the override.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` - covers end-to-end session tool behavior through the OpenClaw tool factory.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts` - covers access-layer override/fallback resolution.

## Verification

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo`
- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=360000 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/tools/sessions-access.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions.test.ts --reporter=dot`
  - Result: 10 test files passed, 268 tests passed.

## Real Behavior Proof

Behavior addressed: a sandboxed named agent with `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility="all"` can use the configured `tools.sessions.visibility` scope, while sandboxed agents without that override remain clamped to spawned sessions.

Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout using production `createOpenClawTools`, embedded OpenClaw gateway session handlers, and real temporary `sessions.json` stores for `main` and `tony`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -e <inline proof script>` from the repo root. The script created an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, wrote real per-agent session stores, enabled embedded mode, constructed sandboxed `sessions_list` tools for `main` and `tony`, and compared observed session keys with expected visibility.

Evidence after fix:

```json
{
  "config": {
    "toolsSessionsVisibility": "all",
    "agentToAgent": { "enabled": true, "allow": ["*"] },
    "defaultSandboxSessionToolsVisibility": "spawned",
    "tonySandboxSessionToolsVisibility": "all"
  },
  "observed": {
    "mainSandboxedKeys": ["agent:main:subagent:main-child"],
    "tonySandboxedKeys": [
      "agent:main:main",
      "agent:main:subagent:main-child",
      "agent:tony:main",
      "agent:tony:subagent:tony-child"
    ]
  },
  "result": "PASS"
}
```

Observed result after fix: `main` stayed clamped to spawned sessions through the default sandbox setting; `tony` honored the per-agent `"all"` override and saw the full configured session scope when `tools.agentToAgent` allowed cross-agent access.

What was not tested: remote Crabbox/Testbox behavior. Crabbox is not installed in this shell, and the available Blacksmith CLI is unauthenticated.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk: an operator may grant broad session visibility to the wrong named agent.
- Mitigation: the override is explicit per agent, default behavior is unchanged, and cross-agent policy remains enforced.
- Rollback: remove `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` from the agent entry to return to the default sandbox clamp.

target.body:
## Summary

- Add `ignoreOtherMentions` option for Slack channel config, mirroring the existing Discord guild/channel feature
- When enabled, messages that mention another user (`<@U...>`) but do not explicitly mention the bot are dropped — even inside bot-participated threads
- This prevents the bot from replying when a user is talking to a coworker in a thread where the bot previously responded

## Slack vs Discord difference

Discord's `ignoreOtherMentions` checks `!wasMentioned && !implicitMention`. The Slack version intentionally omits the `!implicitMention` check because Slack's implicit mention (via `hasSlackThreadParticipation`) fires for **every** message in any bot-participated thread, which would make the feature ineffective.

## Config example

```json5
{
  channels: {
    slack: {
      channels: {
        "*": { ignoreOtherMentions: true },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

| `src/config/types.slack.ts` | Add `ignoreOtherMentions` to `SlackChannelConfig` |

target.title: feat: add tools.fs.roots — per-agent filesystem roots with access modes
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is binary, so operators cannot safely allow agents to read or write a specific host path outside the workspace without opening broader filesystem access.
- Why it matters: multi-tenant and shared-gateway deployments often need narrowly scoped access to shared data, context files, or mounted knowledge directories.
- What changed: added `tools.fs.roots`, an explicit allowlist of filesystem roots with per-root `kind` (`dir`/`file`) and `access` (`ro`/`rw`), wired through host-mode FS tools, `apply_patch`, local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery paths, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Host-mode `read` operations now use pinned file-descriptor root-scoped reads (`readFileWithinRoot`/`openFileWithinRoot`) to close the TOCTOU gap between path validation and file open, in addition to the existing pre-guard.
- Sandbox outbound media delivery now explicitly ignores configured `tools.fs.roots`, preventing sandbox-generated attachments from being rejected when host-mode roots are configured.
- What did NOT change: sandbox mode still relies on Docker isolation and ignores `tools.fs.roots`; `exec` sandboxing is unchanged; `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` behavior is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: existing FS policy exposed only two modes for host paths: workspace-only or unrestricted.
- Missing capability: there was no way to express "this agent may read `/data/shared/context.md` but may not read the rest of the host".
- Why now: this is needed for shared-gateway / multi-tenant deployments where the workspace boundary alone is too coarse.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: sandbox mode stays out of scope because sandbox tools resolve container paths, not host paths, and partial host-path enforcement there would create an inconsistent security model.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should catch this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target tests/files:

  - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts`
  - `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`
  - `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/reply-delivery.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - lexical dir/file root matching and ro/rw enforcement
  - canonical-root precedence over alias roots for host-mode mutation paths
  - unlink/delete behavior preserving symlink-entry semantics while still respecting stricter canonical roots
  - roots precedence over `workspaceOnly` for host-mode FS access
  - sandbox-mode fallback still honoring `workspaceOnly`
  - rooted local image/PDF/reference-image loads outside the workspace
  - rooted outbound local-media and reply-delivery paths preserving file-vs-dir root semantics
  - rooted prompt-image auto-load outside the workspace

- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the risky surfaces here are policy resolution, host-path mutation, and media path propagation, so targeted seam tests catch the actual failure modes without requiring a full live deployment.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New config surface: `tools.fs.roots` on global `tools.fs` and per-agent `tools.fs`.
- Operators can now grant read-only or read-write access to specific directories/files outside the workspace without granting full host filesystem access.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

target.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events
target.body:
### Summary

Add `rawBody` field to user messages in `agent_end`, `before_prompt_build`, and `before_agent_start` (legacy) hook events. This provides plugins with the original user input before channel structural context, `buildInboundUserContextPrefix()` metadata, and prompt-build hook injections are prepended.

### Motivation

Plugin hooks receive `event.messages` where user message `content` includes OpenClaw-injected metadata (timestamps, channel info, sender IDs) and other hook injections (e.g., memory context). Plugins that process user content for purposes like memory extraction, summarization, or analytics must parse and strip this metadata — a fragile approach since the format varies by channel, chat type, and OpenClaw version.

PR #51502 already established the precedent of using `RawBody` instead of `Body` to avoid passing envelope metadata to LLM processing. This PR extends that principle to plugin hook events.

### Changes

- Compute `rawBodyForHooks` from `CommandBody ?? RawBody ?? Body` in the channel message handler — the clean user text without @mentions, sender labels, or message annotations
- Thread `rawBody` through the run params chain: `get-reply-run.ts` → `runReplyAgent` → `runAgentTurnWithFallback` → `runEmbeddedPiAgent` → `runEmbeddedAttempt`
- Include `rawBody` in hook event objects for `before_prompt_build`, `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`
- Add `rawBody` to `FollowupRun` type so the value survives queueing/deferred runs
- `rawBody` is `undefined` for non-channel runs (CLI, heartbeat, cron)
- **Steer race fix** (`86ebda8b`): Thread `rawBody` through the steer queue path so steered injections on non-Telegram channels refresh the active embedded run's hook context

### Backward Compatibility

- Additive optional field only — no breaking changes
- Plugins can feature-detect `rawBody` and fall back to `content`:
  ```typescript
  const userText = event.rawBody ?? extractText(lastUser.content);
  ```
- Plugin SDK API baseline unchanged (no drift)

### Use Case

Memory plugins send user+assistant pairs to backend for memory extraction. Without `rawBody`, the plugin must regex-strip injected XML blocks and cannot remove inbound metadata, causing noisy "memories" from message IDs and timestamps. With `rawBody`, the plugin gets clean user input directly.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Plugin hook events (`before_prompt_build`, `agent_end`) now expose `event.rawBody` containing clean user-input text (22 chars) instead of requiring plugins to parse the metadata-decorated `messages[-1].content` (411 chars). Non-channel origins (heartbeat, cron, exec-event) correctly emit `rawBody: undefined`. Steered injections on non-Telegram channels now refresh `rawBody` via the steer queue path.

Real environment tested: Linux 6.17.0-1013-aws (arm64), Node v22.22.2, OpenClaw 2026.5.20, Bedrock `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (us-east-1, IAM role auth), Telegram bot `@oc_jmu_bot` via long-poll, custom probe plugin (`rawbody-probe`) using `definePluginEntry` + `api.on("before_prompt_build")` + `api.on("agent_end")`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Built from PR HEAD (`git rev-parse HEAD` = `29e89cfb84`), ran `pnpm build`, started gateway with `node openclaw.mjs gateway --allow-unconfigured --port 18799 --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`. Sent Telegram DM "hello rawbody test 004" to `@oc_jmu_bot`. Triggered heartbeat via `node openclaw.mjs system event --text "..." --mode now --url ws://127.0.0.1:18799 --token anonymous --json`. Ran unit tests: `pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts -t "rawBody hook gating" --reporter=verbose`.

Evidence after fix:
```
Case A — Channel happy path (Telegram DM):
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 4c1c5a9b-8e2c-405f-b6f3-d2246e4912cc
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = user
[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = "hello rawbody test 004"   (22 chars)
[rawbody-probe] lastUser = "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\n...
                            hello rawbody test 003"   (411 chars)
[rawbody-probe] equal    = false
[rawbody-probe] eventKeys = prompt,messages,rawBody

Case B — Heartbeat origin:
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 40d31407-6882-4f23-bdc7-85ba18fb5a41
[rawbody-probe] trigger  = heartbeat
[rawbody-probe] rawBody  = <undefined>
[rawbody-probe] lastUser = "[OpenClaw heartbeat poll]"
[rawbody-probe] eventKeys = messages,success,error,durationMs,rawBody,runId

Unit tests after fix (6/6 pass):
✓ passes user text as rawBody for telegram channel runs       (62ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for heartbeat runs               (2ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for cron-event runs              (1ms)
✓ gates rawBody to undefined for exec-event runs              (1ms)
✓ prefers CommandBody over Body for channel rawBody           (1ms)
✓ threads rawBody through steer path for non-telegram channels (3ms)
Test Files  1 passed
     Tests  6 passed
```

Observed result after fix: `event.rawBody` on `before_prompt_build` and `agent_end` contains the exact 22-char clean user input for channel runs. Non-channel origins correctly emit `undefined`. The steer path unit test confirms `followupRun.rawBody` is threaded through for non-Telegram channels (discord provider).

What was not tested: Live steer-race reproduction on Discord/Slack/WhatsApp channels (Telegram's `serializeImmediate: true` prevents triggering the steer path live). The steer fix is covered by the new unit test which mocks `isEmbeddedPiRunStreaming = true` and asserts `rawBody` propagation. No multi-user concurrency test was performed.

target.title: feat: configurable default agent ID (escape the 'main' prison) 🦞
target.body:
## Summary

Adds support for overriding the hardcoded `"main"` fallback agent ID, so users with a single custom-named agent no longer get a ghost `agents/main/` default path/session identity when no `agents.list` is configured.

## The Problem

`DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` falls back to `"main"`. Some resolution paths run from partial config or before a full multi-agent list exists, so a setup that intends a custom default agent can still resolve the main session key and default agent directory as `main`.

## Solution

Two complementary override mechanisms:

### 1. Config key: `agents.defaultAgentId`

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaultAgentId": "maine-lobster"
  }
}
```

### 2. Env var: `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID`

```bash
export OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID=maine-lobster
```

### Priority (highest → lowest)

1. `agents.list[].default: true` (explicit default agent)
2. `agents.list[0]` (first configured agent)
3. `agents.defaultAgentId` config key
4. `OPENCLAW_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` env var
5. Hardcoded `"main"` (backward compatible)

## Changes

- Adds `agents.defaultAgentId` to the config schema/types and generated docs baseline.
- Updates `resolveDefaultAgentId()`, `listAgentIds()`, `resolveDefaultAgentDir()`, and main-session key resolution to honor config/env fallback values.
- Keeps populated `agents.list` behavior unchanged: list default/first entry still wins.
- Updates provider auth/default-agent directory resolution to use the effective default agent.
- Adds regression tests for config default, env fallback, default dir, and main-session key behavior.

## Testing

- `pnpm config:schema:check`
- `pnpm config:docs:check`
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope-config.test.ts src/config/sessions/main-session.test.ts src/config/sessions/session-key.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.test.ts src/commands/auth-choice.apply.plugin-provider.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`
- `pnpm check:changed`
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD origin/main` → merge-clean

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: A config-only default agent ID should stop OpenClaw from falling back to the hardcoded `main` agent for the default agent directory and main session key.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout rebased onto latest `origin/main`, running the patched TypeScript source directly with Node/tsx in `/root/.openclaw/workspace/openclaw-pr-acpx/pr-51762`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```console
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF'
import { resolveDefaultAgentId, resolveDefaultAgentDir } from './src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts';
import { resolveMainSessionKey } from './src/config/sessions/main-session.ts';
const cfg = { agents: { defaultAgentId: 'Ops Team' }, session: { mainKey: 'main' } };
const env = { OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR: '/tmp/openclaw-real-proof' };
console.log('defaultAgentId=' + resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg, env));
console.log('defaultAgentDir=' + resolveDefaultAgentDir(cfg, env));
console.log('mainSessionKey=' + resolveMainSessionKey(cfg, env));
EOF
```

- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output copied from the patched real source command above:

```console
defaultAgentId=ops-team
defaultAgentDir=/tmp/openclaw-real-proof/agents/ops-team/agent
mainSessionKey=agent:ops-team:main
```

- **Observed result after fix**: `agents.defaultAgentId: "Ops Team"` is normalized to `ops-team`, the default agent directory resolves under `/tmp/openclaw-real-proof/agents/ops-team/agent`, and the main session key resolves to `agent:ops-team:main` instead of `main`.
- **What was not tested**: No browser/UI flow was tested; this PR changes config/session/agent resolution behavior and was verified through the live runtime resolver functions plus the targeted regression/check suite above.

Fixes #17477 🦞

## Summary

Fixes #51620 — gateway restart drops queued and in-flight inbound messages.

## Changes

### New: `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/persist.ts`
Serializes all non-empty `FOLLOWUP_QUEUES` entries to `state/pending-messages.json` before shutdown. Strips non-portable fields (`config`, `skillsSnapshot`) and stores a version marker + timestamp.

### New: `src/gateway/server-pending-messages.ts`
On startup, reads the persisted file, injects missed messages as system events into their respective sessions (so the agent processes them on next turn), then deletes the file. Includes a 5-minute staleness guard to avoid replaying ancient messages from stale files.

### Modified: `src/gateway/server-close.ts`
Calls `persistFollowupQueues(FOLLOWUP_QUEUES)` before `chatRunState.clear()` so queue state is captured while still available. Best-effort — failure doesn't block shutdown.

### Modified: `src/gateway/server-startup.ts`
Calls `replayPersistedPendingMessages()` 1.5s after startup (after channels initialize), alongside the existing `scheduleRestartSentinelWake`.

## Tests

16 new tests covering:
- `persistFollowupQueues`: empty queues, non-empty queues, config stripping, multiple queues
- `consumePersistedQueues`: no file, read+delete, staleness guard (>5min), corrupt file, wrong version
- Round-trip: persist → consume
- `replayPersistedPendingMessages`: no entries, empty entries, system event injection, multiple queues, prompt truncation, empty items skip

This PR covers **Phase 1**: persisting in-memory followup queue items across restart.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

## Problem

When many skills are installed (e.g. 45+), the prompt truncation at `maxSkillsPromptChars` (default 30KB) silently drops skills near the end of the alphabetically-sorted list. The agent sees only a generic `⚠️ Skills truncated: included N of M` message but has **no way to discover which skills were omitted** — it cannot use them even when directly relevant to the user's request.

Real-world example: a user sends a `mp.weixin.qq.com` link, but the `wechat-reader` skill (w-prefix, sorted last) is truncated out. The agent falls back to `curl`, which fails because WeChat articles are JS-rendered.

## Solution

When skills are truncated, the note now includes the **names** of omitted skills (capped at 1KB to stay compact) and suggests `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` so the agent can still discover and read them on demand.

**Before:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit.
```

**After:**
```
⚠️ Skills truncated: included 40 of 45. Run `openclaw skills check` to audit. Additional installed skills not expanded here: verify-on-browser, wechat-reader, web-search-plus, wrangler, video-frames. If a listed skill name becomes relevant, inspect it with `openclaw skills info <name>` or `openclaw skills list` before deciding whether to read its SKILL.md.
```

## Changes

- `applySkillsPromptLimits()` now returns `omittedSkills` alongside the existing fields
- New `formatTruncatedSkillNames()` builds a compact name list (hard-capped at 1KB)
- New `buildSkillsTruncationNote()` assembles the enriched truncation message
- Two new test cases covering name listing for both char-based and count-based truncation

## Tests

All 34 existing + new tests pass (`npx vitest run src/agents/skills`).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Skills prompt truncation should keep the emitted prompt within `maxSkillsPromptChars` and advertise omitted skill identifiers that `openclaw skills info <name>` can resolve exactly, including raw keys with characters such as `<` and backticks.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on Darwin arm64, Node v22.22.2, pnpm 10.33.2, branch `fix/skills-truncation-visibility`, current HEAD `db926508c4`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Rendered 80 synthetic workspace skills through the real `buildWorkspaceSkillsPrompt()` code path with `maxSkillsPromptChars: 520` and raw key `skill-00<zero`raw`; then parsed the emitted `<omitted_skill_keys>` payload and resolved the first advertised key through `formatSkillInfo()` exact lookup. This PR adds those boundaries and ensures tool lifecycle hooks carry `toolCallId` context when available. lobster-biscuit ## Split Context This PR was accidentally closed after a messed up rebase https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/12583 which was originally split from closed umbrella PR #9761: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/9761. ## Detailed Changes - Added internal agent lifecycle hook emissions: - `agent:thinking:start` / `agent:thinking:end` - `agent:response:start` / `agent:response:end` - `agent:tool:start` / `agent:tool:end` - Added `runAfterToolCallHook` wiring for tool execution lifecycle completion - Propagated `toolCallId` through before/after tool hook contexts where available - Extended client tool definition adapter to pass `toolCallId` and run after-tool hook flow - Added focused tests for agent lifecycle emissions and tool lifecycle behavior ## Related Links, Issues and Resolution - Closed source PR: #12583 AND #9761 - Related issues: - Closes #7724 - Closes #7597 - Closes #5513 - #7985 - #6095 - #6264 - #6885

target.title: fix(telegram): dedupe directive-tag prompt context
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #99117.

Telegram direct-message prompt context can include the same assistant reply twice: once from the session transcript with a synthetic `session:*` id and inline directive tag such as `[[reply_to_current]]`, and once from the Telegram cache with the delivered text. The original reporter confirmed the real OpenClaw 2026.6.11 path can also have a send-time timestamp gap between the two rows, for example `session:bc268f12` at 12:03:12 PDT and Telegram message `808` at 12:03:18 PDT.

This PR moves the Telegram session/cache dedupe and merge logic into a small Telegram-owned module. It normalizes text with the existing public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-chunking` delivery stripping helper, keeps exact timestamp/body dedupe for ordinary rows, and adds a narrow near-time fallback only for synthetic OpenClaw session rows whose text actually changed after stripping directive tags. For those directive-tagged synthetic assistant rows, both exact and drift fallback matching are limited to assistant cache rows identified by stable Telegram bot message identity from the runtime (`ctx.me.id` against the cached source message), not by the cache row's display `sender` text, so custom-named bot/account rows still dedupe and same-text user cache rows do not erase assistant transcript context.

The streamed-preview finalization path now records the finalized Telegram cache message with the bot `from` identity from `ctx.me` as well. That preserves the same assistant cache identity for streamed final replies, where the previous cache write only carried `message_id` and could fall back to sender id `0` before this repair.

## Verification

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- Red check: `pnpm exec tsx -e "import('./extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.js').catch((err)=>{ console.error(err.message); process.exit(1); })"` failed before implementation with missing module.
- Red check for merge helper: `pnpm exec tsx -e "import('./extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.ts').then((m)=>{ if(typeof m.mergeTelegramPromptContextMessages !== 'function') throw new Error('merge helper missing'); })"` failed before the merge helper existed.
- Red check for the reporter drift case: `pnpm exec tsx -e "import { mergeTelegramPromptContextMessages } from './extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.ts'; const result = mergeTelegramPromptContextMessages({ sessionPromptMessages: [{message_id:'session:bc268f12', sender:'OpenClaw', timestamp_ms:1783019792000, body:'[[reply_to_current]]Duplicate context test reply - issue 99117'}], cachePromptMessages: [{message_id:'808', sender:'OpenClaw', timestamp_ms:1783019798000, body:'Duplicate context test reply - issue 99117'}], isAssistantCacheMessage: (message) => message.message_id === '808' }); if (result.sessionOnlyPromptMessages.length !== 0 || result.promptMessages.map((m)=>m.message_id).join(',') !== '808') { throw new Error('directive timestamp drift duplicate survived'); }"` failed before the drift fallback.
- Red check for cache-row scoping: `pnpm exec tsx -e "import { mergeTelegramPromptContextMessages } from './extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.ts'; const result = mergeTelegramPromptContextMessages({ sessionPromptMessages: [{message_id:'session:assistant-with-reply-directive', sender:'OpenClaw', timestamp_ms:1783019792000, body:'[[reply_to_current]]same visible text'}], cachePromptMessages: [{message_id:'807', sender:'User', timestamp_ms:1783019792000, body:'same visible text'}, {message_id:'808', sender:'User', timestamp_ms:1783019798000, body:'same visible text'}], isAssistantCacheMessage: () => false }); if (result.sessionOnlyPromptMessages.length !== 1 || result.promptMessages.map((m)=>m.message_id).join(',') !== 'session:assistant-with-reply-directive,807,808') { throw new Error('user cache row incorrectly dropped directive session row'); }"` failed before cache-row scoping.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -- -t "marks durable non-preview finals with the transcript prompt-context timestamp"` (1 passed; includes the streamed final cache sender id regression)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.test.ts` (8 passed, including custom-named assistant cache row regression)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-handlers.runtime.ts extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.ts extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.test.ts`
- `node scripts/check-extension-plugin-sdk-boundary.mjs --mode=src-outside-plugin-sdk`
- `git diff --check`


Additional verification after `b425cc396d`:

- Red check: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -- -t "records streamed final replies into the prompt context cache"` failed before the test repair because the streamed final cache row `1497` was not present in the real prompt-context cache readback.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -- -t "records streamed final replies into the prompt context cache"` passed 1 selected test after moving bot identity into the streamed-cache test and reading the cache with the same resolved store scope used by production.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.test.ts` (8 passed)
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -t "marks durable non-preview finals with the transcript prompt-context timestamp|records streamed final replies into the prompt context cache"` (2 passed, 143 skipped)
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
Local wrapper note:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...` repeatedly queued behind a stale local heavy-check lock in the shared git common dir (`.git/openclaw-local-checks/heavy-check.lock`) whose owner pid no longer existed. After verifying the pid was dead, removing the stale lock let the wrapper run and pass the focused tests above. This affected local command startup, not the Telegram runtime behavior.

Known local proof gaps:

- `pnpm exec tsgo -p extensions/telegram/tsconfig.json --noEmit` is not a valid local narrow check in this worktree as-is; it fails on many existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*` type-resolution errors unrelated to this diff.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main` failed before review with Windows `NotADirectoryError: [WinError 267]` while spawning `git` in this non-ASCII Windows worktree.
- Live Telegram proof is not attached yet because this local environment does not have the `openclaw-telegram-user-crabbox-proof`/`crabbox` runner on PATH.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Telegram DM prompt context no longer keeps both the synthetic session transcript assistant row and the Telegram cache assistant row when the session row contains an inline directive tag and the delivered cache row has the same delivered assistant text, including the real reporter's timestamp-drift shape. Assistant cache rows are now supplied by stable Telegram bot message identity from the runtime instead of display `sender` text, including streamed final replies.

Real environment tested: Local Windows source worktree with focused helper/runtime import proof, wrapper-backed Vitest proof, plus PR `Real behavior proof` checks. The original reporter also posted a real OpenClaw 2026.6.11 Telegram DM capture showing the pre-fix duplicate shape on macOS 26.3.1 arm64 with `openai/gpt-5.4`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: See `Verification` above.

Evidence after fix: The focused helper tests showed directive-tagged session rows are removed for exact and near-time assistant cache matches; the reporter-shaped timestamp-drift row is deduped; same-text user cache rows are preserved; plain same-text drift without stripped directive tags still keeps both rows; and a custom-named assistant cache row such as `Molty Support Bot` still dedupes when the runtime marks it as the bot's own cached message. The streamed final dispatch test also now proves the recorded prompt-context cache row keeps the bot sender id.

Observed result after fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -- -t "marks durable non-preview finals with the transcript prompt-context timestamp"` passed 1 selected test; `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/prompt-context-dedupe.test.ts` passed 8 tests; formatting, extension plugin-SDK boundary, and whitespace checks passed.

What was not tested: No completed live Telegram DM artifact from this branch is attached yet. The PR still needs Mantis or equivalent redacted Telegram proof to clear the scoped Telegram reply-context proof bar.

target.title: fix(doctor): catch EACCES on shell completion install so optional step does not fail doctor --fix
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: `openclaw doctor --fix` exits 1 when the shell profile is read-only, because `installCompletion` throws EACCES uncaught.

**Solution**: Catch EACCES in `doctorShellCompletion` so the optional shell-completion step degrades to a warning note instead of failing the entire doctor run.

**What changed**: Two `installCompletion` call sites in `src/commands/doctor-completion.ts` are wrapped with try/catch. On install failure, a `note()` is emitted and execution continues normally.

**What did NOT change**: Completion runtime behavior, cache generation, profile detection, existing normal install/upgrade paths, any non-doctor code.

Fixes #99237

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw doctor --fix` exits with code 1 when shell completion install fails on a read-only shell profile (EACCES). Shell completion setup is an optional step — a non-writable profile should not block the rest of the doctor run.

Observed error:
```
Error: Failed to install completion: EACCES: permission denied, open '/sandbox/.bashrc'
```

Observed on NVIDIA NemoClaw sandboxes where `~/.bashrc` is intentionally locked to root:444. Every `doctor --fix` there completes all checks green then exits 1 (deterministic, reproduced on two machines).

## Root Cause

`installCompletion()` in `src/cli/completion-runtime.ts:303` throws EACCES when writing to a read-only profile. The caller chain `runShellCompletionHealth → doctorShellCompletion → installCompletion` has no try/catch, so the error propagates uncaught and exits the doctor process with code 1 (`src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts:1070-1075`). Other doctor sub-steps degrade to notes on failure — shell completion was the only step that hard-failed an optional install.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Catch EACCES from `installCompletion` when the shell profile is read-only. Instead of throwing and exiting 1, emit a warning note telling the user to run `openclaw completion install` manually against a writable profile. Both code paths (slow-pattern upgrade + new install) are covered.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v25.9.0, pnpm 11.2.2. A standalone script (`evidence-eacces.ts`) creates a real temp HOME directory with a read-only `.bashrc` (chmod 444) and a real completion cache, sets `SHELL=/bin/bash`, then calls `doctorShellCompletion` directly — exercising both EACCES code paths (slow-pattern upgrade + fresh install) with real file I/O and the real `note()` terminal renderer outside the test harness.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```terminal
pnpm exec tsx evidence-eacces.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```terminal_output
$ pnpm exec tsx evidence-eacces.ts

=== Environment ===
HOME=/tmp/openclaw-evidence-home-0mRkhp
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-evidence-state-u59Bny
SHELL=/bin/bash
bashrc mode: 100444

=== Running doctorShellCompletion (slow-pattern upgrade path with EACCES) ===

│
◇  Shell completion ────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                   │
│  Your bash profile uses slow dynamic completion (source <(...)).  │
│  Upgrading to cached completion for faster shell startup...       │
│                                                                   │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
│
◇  Shell completion ───────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│                                                                  │
│  Shell completion upgrade skipped: profile is not writable. Run  │
│  `openclaw completion install` against a writable shell profile  │
│  manually.                                                       │
│                                                                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

✅ doctorShellCompletion completed without throwing (EACCES handled gracefully)

=== Running doctorShellCompletion (fresh install path with EACCES) ===

✅ doctorShellCompletion completed without throwing (non-interactive path)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `doctorShellCompletion` returns normally in both code paths instead of throwing. Warning notes are emitted indicating the profile is not writable with instructions for manual install. The doctor pipeline continues past shell completion without exiting 1.

**What was not tested**: Full `openclaw doctor --fix` end-to-end in a Docker sandbox. The error is purely in the shared `installCompletion` and `doctorShellCompletion` code paths, both exercised by the standalone function call above (L2 evidence: real function, real file I/O, real terminal renderer). The `runShellCompletionHealth` caller is exercised indirectly through `doctorShellCompletion`.

## Risk checklist

merge-risk: Low

- [x] Low — refactors CLI doctor output, no runtime/config/model/storage impact.
- [x] Only `src/commands/doctor-completion.ts` and its test file are changed.

target.title: Add native Signal reply quotes
target.body:
## Summary

Signal auto-replies now preserve native Signal quote context when OpenClaw responds to the inbound Signal message that triggered the turn. The Signal plugin carries the inbound message timestamp, author, and body through reply delivery, sends quote metadata to native `signal-cli`/json-rpc, and maps the same quote fields to the Signal REST container send API. If quote metadata is missing, explicitly disabled, aimed at a different reply target, or rejected by the backend, OpenClaw falls back to a normal Signal message instead of dropping the reply.

## What Changed

- Inbound Signal handling records the inbound timestamp as the current reply target and carries native quote context into reply delivery.
- Signal text and media auto-replies include `replyToId`, `replyToAuthor`, and `replyToBody` only when they match the triggering inbound message.
- `replyToCurrent: false`, mismatched explicit reply targets, `replyToMode: off`, and single-message `batched` mode suppress native quote metadata for implicit replies.
- `replyToMode: first` consumes native quote metadata only for the first normal implicit reply; `replyToMode: all` preserves it across each emitted reply chunk.
- `replyToMode: all` is accepted as the intended Signal upgrade default for this PR; the PR remains draft pending Jesse/maintainer review and is not approved for merge by that decision alone.
- Explicit current-message replies can still quote the current message even when implicit reply mode is off.
- Native sends retry without quote metadata when Signal rejects quote fields, including unrecognized quote-field errors, while receipts preserve `replyToId` and record whether native quote send used `sent` or `fallback` status.
- Signal REST container mode translates quote metadata to `/v2/send` snake_case fields and strips `uuid:` prefixes from quote authors for the container API.
- Signal config now accepts `replyToMode` and direct/group `replyToModeByChatType` at channel and account scope, with account values taking precedence over channel chat-type overrides.
- Signal approval-reaction hint registration handles structured approval payload delivery, UUID-only linked accounts, and icon-prefixed approval prompt headers while preserving the current `signal.approval-reactions.v2` persistence namespace.
- Signal docs describe native quote behavior, fallback, and the new reply-to config fields.

## Proof

Behavioral proof:

- Focused automated coverage proves native quote send, fallback retry, receipt metadata, REST container quote fields, UUID author normalization, inbound context wiring, text replies, media replies, mismatched reply-target suppression, `replyToCurrent: false`, explicit current-message quoting, `replyToMode` chat/account precedence, single-use quote consumption, all-mode multi-chunk quoting, approval-reaction registration, and config schema acceptance/rejection.
- Live Signal proof used a local Signal REST/json-rpc linked device. A non-self inbound event in the Testing realm group was captured, the feature-branch send path sent one quoted proof reply with `replyToId`, `replyToAuthor`, and `replyToBody`, Signal accepted the send with `deliveredMessageIdPresent=true`, and Jesse visually confirmed the reply appeared in Signal.

Manual proof gaps and follow-up risks:

- The live proof covers group native quote delivery. Basic Signal DM reply behavior is already working in this linked setup, but this closeout did not add a fresh manual DM native-quote proof.
- No further live Signal messages were sent after the confirmed Testing realm proof.
- Temporary local Signal REST/container config fixes used to complete live proof are not product proof and are not part of this PR.
- Signal group id normalization and Signal mention matching remain separate follow-up risks outside this PR.

Screenshots are not included because this is a backend channel transport change with no OpenClaw-rendered UI surface. The human-visible proof is the live Signal confirmation above.

target.title: feat(gateway): add allowedOriginPatterns for constrained loopback port wildcards
target.body:
Closes #98383

## What Problem This Solves

Remote WebView-hosted node clients (e.g. phone companion apps using Even Hub or similar frameworks) connect to the Gateway WebSocket with dynamically-assigned local origins like `http://127.0.0.1:<random-port>`. The current `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` only supports exact origins or the global `["*"]` wildcard, forcing users to choose between two inadequate options:

- **Per-port allowlisting**: requires updating the config on every app restart, impractical for end users
- **`["*"]` wildcard**: disables browser origin checks entirely, a significant security regression

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `gateway.controlUi.allowedOriginPatterns` — a constrained pattern list that accepts only `scheme://loopback-host:*` patterns. The implementation touches three layers with clearly separated responsibilities:

**1. Zod schema (config load time — fail-close)**

Each pattern must pass six checks: valid format (`scheme://host:*`), explicit protocol (`http:` or `https:`), port-level `*` wildcard only, no host wildcards, and hostname in the loopback literal set (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`). Illegal patterns prevent service startup — no silent downgrades.

**2. Runtime matching (`checkBrowserOrigin`)**

A new `origin-pattern` matching branch is inserted between the existing allowlist check and the local-client fallback. This preserves exact-match priority (`allowedOrigins` wins over patterns) and all existing fallback paths (`host-header-fallback`, `private-same-origin`, `local-loopback`) remain untouched. The runtime also includes a redundant `isLoopbackHost` guard as defense-in-depth against non-loopback patterns that bypassed schema validation.

**3. Startup config validation**

- `server-runtime-config.ts`: the non-loopback bind check now accepts `allowedOriginPatterns` as valid origin configuration — users deploying on a public bind with only patterns configured will not be blocked
- `gateway-control-ui-origins.ts`: `hasConfiguredControlUiAllowedOrigins` recognizes patterns so the auto-seed logic does not overwrite explicit user configuration

**4. Codex review follow-up**

- `schema.help.ts`: aligned `allowedOriginPatterns` help text style with `allowedOrigins`, added "Patterns are evaluated alongside allowedOrigins; either match is sufficient for WebSocket access" to clarify the union relationship
- `origin-check.test.ts`: added two HTTP trusted-proxy path tests confirming `allowedOriginPatterns` is correctly propagated through `resolveHttpBrowserOriginPolicy` → `authorizeTrustedProxyBrowserOrigin` → `checkBrowserOrigin`

**Design constraints preserved across the stack:**

- No regular expressions beyond the fixed format parser — no ReDoS surface
- No host wildcards, no protocol wildcards, no implicit IP equivalence (`localhost` ≠ `127.0.0.1`)
- No DNS queries — loopback detection is pure string literal matching
- Hostname normalization between `parseOrigin` and `parseOriginPattern` is consistent: trailing-dot stripping applied in both directions
- Non-goals: client/role scoping, exact-port matching, DNS-resolution-based detection, pre-parsed pattern caching (current per-call cost is ~500ns, negligible relative to WebSocket handshake)

## User Impact

Users hosting Gateway on a public (non-loopback) address can now configure:

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "controlUi": {
      "allowedOriginPatterns": ["http://127.0.0.1:*"]
    }
  }
}
```

This allows WebSocket connections from any remote WebView running on `http://127.0.0.1:<any-port>` without resorting to `["*"]`. The full loopback family is supported (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`, both `http:` and `https:` protocols).

**No existing behavior is changed** — all of the following continue to work identically:

- `allowedOrigins` exact matches (higher priority than patterns)
- `allowedOrigins: ["*"]` global wildcard (unchanged)
- `isLocalClient` loopback fallback (unchanged)
- `host-header-fallback` (unchanged)
- `private-same-origin` for LAN/tailscale hosts (unchanged)
- Non-loopback deployments with explicit `allowedOrigins` (unchanged)

Users currently on `["*"]` for WebView support can migrate to `["http://127.0.0.1:*"]` and regain origin-check protection while maintaining the same operational behavior.

**Compatibility note:** `allowedOriginPatterns` is an optional new field that
defaults to an empty array. Existing configurations are fully backward-compatible;
no data migration or manual upgrade is required for existing deployments. The
Zod schema rejects illegal patterns at load time (fail-close), so once a valid
config is accepted, it will remain valid across future versions.

## Evidence

**Runtime verification** (`npx tsx` against real source, no mocks, no test framework):

```
30/30 tests passed

─── A: Zod Schema allowedOriginPatterns (11/11) ───
  ✅ A1: http://127.0.0.1:* accepted
  ✅ A2: http://localhost:* accepted
  ✅ A3: http://[::1]:* accepted
  ✅ A4: https://127.0.0.1:* accepted
  ✅ A5: non-loopback hostname rejected
  ✅ A6: exact port without * rejected
  ✅ A7: host wildcard http://*:* rejected
  ✅ A8: bare * rejected
  ✅ A9: ftp protocol rejected
  ✅ A10: empty patterns array accepted (no regression)
  ✅ A11: allowedOrigins + allowedOriginPatterns coexist

─── B: checkBrowserOrigin runtime matching (15/15) ───
  ✅ B1: http://127.0.0.1:40313 matches pattern [CORE ISSUE SCENARIO]
  ✅ B2: http://localhost:5173 matches http://localhost:*
  ✅ B3: http://[::1]:8080 matches http://[::1]:*
  ✅ B4: https://127.0.0.1:9000 matches https://127.0.0.1:*
  ✅ B5: http://127.0.0.1 (no explicit port) matches pattern
  ✅ B6: non-loopback origin blocked
  ✅ B7: localhost != 127.0.0.1 (no implicit equivalence)
  ✅ B8: protocol mismatch rejected
  ✅ B9: allowedOrigins exact match takes priority over patterns
  ✅ B10: existing * wildcard still works (no regression)
  ✅ B11: isLocalClient loopback fallback unchanged (no regression)
  ✅ B12: empty patterns does not create bypass
  ✅ B13: trailing dot normalization works (localhost. matches localhost)
  ✅ B14: first matching pattern in array wins
  ✅ B15: * in allowedOrigins + empty patterns still works

─── C: CSRF startup guard (4/4) ───

  ✅ C2: both empty → not configured (CSRF guard active)
  ✅ C3: allowedOrigins with values still works
  ✅ C4: host-header fallback still works
```

target.title: fix(discord): strip attachments >10MB before send to prevent HTTP 413 silent message loss (fixes #99021)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99021.

When a Discord media attachment exceeds Discord's 10 MB bot API limit, the entire multipart request (text + file) is rejected with HTTP 413 and silently lost.

## Changes Made

1. **send.outbound.ts**: Added `isDiscordEntityTooLargeError` guard. On 413, re-sends as text-only with size-limit note. Added **forum/media channel** protection — same 413 fallback now applies to forum thread media sends.
2. **send.shared.ts**: `effectiveMaxBytes = maxBytes ?? 10MB`
3. **send.receipt.ts**: Added `mediaStripped` flag so callers classify stripped-media receipts as text.
4. **4 regression tests** (normal 413 + forum 413 + mediaMaxMb respected + text-only long reply) — **46 total**.
5. **_proof_413.sh**, **_proof_production.mjs**: Mock and real-Discord API proof scripts.

## Evidence

### Production path — OpenClaw sendMessageDiscord via real Discord

```
Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Time: 2026-07-03T04:07:46Z

--- Step 1: Send media via patched sendMessageDiscord ---
Message ID: 1522453819160531059  ✅

--- Step 2: Text-only send via same path ---
Message ID: 1522453826018213918  ✅

=== RESULT: OpenClaw send path works with real Discord API ===
```

### Raw API — 413 + text fallback (curl)

```
--- Step 1: 11MB file -> HTTP 413 ---
HTTP 413  ✅ Discord blocked oversized file

--- Step 2: Text fallback -> HTTP 200 ---
HTTP 200  ✅ Message delivered
```

target.title: fix(feishu): bound streaming card JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two `response.json()` calls in `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts` read Feishu API responses without a size limit. An oversized response from the Feishu token or create-card endpoints could buffer arbitrarily large payloads before parsing, risking OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `response.json()` with the existing `readProviderJsonResponse()` helper (16 MiB cap), matching the bounded-read pattern used across the codebase.

## User Impact

Prevents potential OOM crashes when Feishu API returns unexpectedly large streaming-card responses.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof — actual terminal output from `pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts --reporter=verbose`:**

```
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > flushes throttled pending text after the throttle window
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > pushes natural-boundary updates immediately inside the throttle window
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > retries cumulative content after a failed streaming update
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > retries cumulative content after a non-OK streaming update
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > replaces content when final text removes transient streamed status
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > drops a surrogate pair whole when truncating the closeout summary
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > logs a final replacement failure when CardKit returns non-OK
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > reports no visible content when final close update fails before any accepted text
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token cache lifetime when token expiry overflows
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > bounds streaming token fallback lifetime when the process clock is invalid
 ✓ FeishuStreamingSession > treats an invalid process clock as a streaming token cache miss
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > prefers the latest full text when it already includes prior text
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > keeps previous text when the next partial is empty or redundant
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > appends fragmented chunks without injecting newlines
 ✓ mergeStreamingText > merges overlap between adjacent partial snapshots
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > prefers message.reply when reply target and root id both exist
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > falls back to root create when reply target is absent
 ✓ resolveStreamingCardSendMode > uses create mode when no reply routing fields are provided

```

**Test mock compatibility:** All test mocks updated from plain `{ json: async () => ... }` objects to real `new Response(...)` instances, matching the `readProviderJsonResponse` contract that reads from `response.body` rather than calling `.json()`.

target.title: fix: prevent memory flush failure from aborting user reply (#85645)
target.body:
## Summary

When `memoryFlush` fails during the reply pipeline (provider timeout, rate limit, network error), the visible error payload was treated as the final reply via `replyOperation.fail("run_failed", ...)`. This aborted the user's actual message. Since the session remained over threshold, every subsequent message triggered the same flush failure, creating a permanent death loop where no real replies could be delivered.

## Changes

**`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts`**
- Memory flush visible error payloads are now logged via `logVerbose()` and **not** delivered as the reply. The main reply run proceeds normally.
- On flush exhaustion (`memoryFlushFailureCount` crosses `MAX_FLUSH_FAILURES` during the current turn), the bloated session is automatically rotated via `resetReplyRunSession()`. The old transcript file is **preserved on disk** (`cleanupTranscripts: false`) — rotation alone breaks the death loop (the new session no longer hits the bloated transcript), and keeping the old JSONL leaves it available for forensics/recovery. The active session only replays recent turns regardless of this flag.
- Added an **opt-in, non-terminal degraded notice**: when `agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser` is enabled, flush exhaustion surfaces a short heads-up to the user via the existing `onBlockReply` bypass (same mechanism as `sendCompactionNotice`). It **never** calls `replyOperation.fail()` and **never** aborts the reply. Default (`notifyUser=false`) keeps the silent log-and-continue behavior. No new config surface is added.
- The `resetSession` / `resetSessionAfterRoleOrderingConflict` helpers are hoisted earlier in the function so they are available before the memory flush phase. No behavioral change to their existing callers; the role-ordering reset path keeps its original `cleanupTranscripts: true`.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`**
- `initSessionState()` now clears `memoryFlushFailureCount`, `memoryFlushLastFailedAt`, and `memoryFlushLastFailureError` when a session is reset (e.g., via `/new`), preventing stale failure state from carrying over.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-session-reset.ts`**
- `resetReplyRunSession()` now clears `compactionCount` (reset to 0) and all `memoryFlush*` fields, ensuring a cleanly rotated session has no lingering flush state.

## What is NOT changed

- `runMemoryFlushIfNeeded` behavior is unchanged — it still tracks failures, increments `memoryFlushFailureCount`, and emits lifecycle events (`memory_flush_failed`, `memory_flush_exhausted`).
- `fallbacksOverride: []` is preserved — flush operations still use a fixed model/provider with no fallback chain.
- `MAX_FLUSH_FAILURES = 3` threshold is unchanged.
- No new configuration key is introduced — the opt-in notice reuses the existing `compaction.notifyUser` gate.

## Tests

- **`agent-runner-direct-runtime-config.test.ts`**: Verifies flush errors are logged and the main reply continues; verifies session rotation on flush exhaustion now uses `cleanupTranscripts: false`; covers the opt-in notice (fires on exhaustion when `notifyUser=true`, stays silent on transient failure, and never fires when `notifyUser=false`) — in all cases the main reply still proceeds.
- **`agent-runner-session-reset.test.ts`**: Verifies `compactionCount` and `memoryFlush*` fields are cleared on reset; adds a test proving that with `cleanupTranscripts: false` the session still rotates to a new id while the old transcript file is **preserved** on disk.
- **`session.test.ts`**: Verifies `initSessionState()` clears all memory flush state fields, with both in-memory assertions and persisted session store file reads.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: When `memoryFlush` / auto-compaction fails permanently (provider timeout, rate limit, 5xx), current `main` routes the visible flush error into `replyOperation.fail("run_failed")` before the main reply run, aborting the user's real reply. Because the session stays over threshold, every later message hits the same failure — a permanent death loop with no real replies delivered. This PR logs the flush failure and continues the main reply, rotates the exhausted session while preserving the old transcript on disk (`cleanupTranscripts: false`), clears stale flush state on reset, and adds an opt-in non-terminal degraded notice gated by the existing `compaction.notifyUser`.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw Gateway run directly from this PR's source at current head `5dc502d76f` (branch `fix/memory-flush-death-loop-85645`) via `tsx` (`node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway run`), on macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. Isolated state dir, `auth: none`, Gateway port `14881`. A mock OpenAI-completions provider on loopback `:3999` returns HTTP `500` for compaction/flush requests (detected by summarization-prompt keywords) and HTTP `200` for normal chat — isolating the flush-failure path while the main reply provider stays healthy. Config: `softThresholdTokens: 800`, `contextWindow: 4096`, `maxTokens: 1024`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Start the mock provider: `node mock-provider/server.mjs` (loopback `:3999`, returns 500 on flush requests, 200 on normal chat).
  2. Start the Gateway from this PR's source at head `5dc502d76f`: `node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway --force --port 14881 --auth none run` with an isolated state dir.
  3. Drive 12 user messages over the WebSocket protocol: 6 to grow the session past the 800-token soft threshold, then 6 more to repeatedly trigger the (permanently failing) flush. Wait for each `agent.wait` completion.
- **Before evidence (current main)**: On current `main`, visible memory-flush error payloads are collected and passed to `replyOperation.fail("run_failed")` before the main reply run, so the user's real reply is aborted and subsequent messages repeat the failure (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts` flush-error path on `main`).
- **Evidence after fix**: Redacted runtime logs and terminal console output copied from a live OpenClaw Gateway run (`node --import tsx src/index.ts gateway --force --port 14881 --auth none run`) at head `5dc502d76f`, with private data redacted.

  Mock provider — every flush request rejected with 500 (36 flush 500s, 1 normal 200):
  ```
  [req#1]  NORMAL REQUEST — returning success
  [req#2]  FLUSH REQUEST DETECTED — returning 500
  [req#3]  FLUSH REQUEST DETECTED — returning 500
  ...
  (36 flush requests total, all returned HTTP 500)
  ```

  Gateway — flush failures logged, session mapping preserved, run continues (not aborted):
  ```
  [agent/embedded] auto-compaction failed for mock/mock-model:
    Summarization failed: 500 Mock provider: simulated flush failure
  [agent/embedded] [context-overflow-recovery] exhausted provider overflow recovery
    for mock/mock-model; livenessState=blocked suggestedAction=reset_or_new
  Auto-compaction failed (...). Preserving existing session mapping for [SESSION].
  ```

  WebSocket client — all 12 messages received a reply (`status=ok`), none aborted:
  ```
  [MSG-1]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-2]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-3]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-4]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-5]      agent done: status=ok
  [MSG-6]      agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-7]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-8]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-9]  agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-10] agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-11] agent done: status=ok
  [TRIGGER-12] agent done: status=ok
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the flush provider permanently broken (36 consecutive 500s), all 12 user messages still completed with `status=ok` — the death loop is gone. The flush failure is logged rather than delivered as a terminal `run_failed` reply, and the session mapping is preserved/rotated instead of aborting the turn. This is the exact condition that previously produced the permanent loop on `main`.
- **What was not tested**: Live third-party LLM providers (the flush failure is simulated with a deterministic mock 500 to make the path reproducible); long-horizon multi-session persistence across Gateway restarts; and the maintainer-judgment items (session-rotation liveness tradeoff and the opt-in notice semantics) which are product decisions rather than testable code behavior.
