target.title: fix(anthropic): add claude-sonnet-5 to bundled 1M-context catalog
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`) ships from Anthropic with a 1,000,000-token
context window as both default and maximum, but the bundled Anthropic catalog and
the GA-1M prefix allow-list predate the model, so nothing recognizes it:

- `extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.json` has no `claude-sonnet-5` entry under
  either the `anthropic` or `claude-cli` provider.
- `ANTHROPIC_GA_1M_MODEL_PREFIXES` — duplicated in `src/agents/context-resolution.ts`
  and `extensions/anthropic/stream-wrappers.ts` — does not list the model.

As a result `resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow()` returns `undefined` for
`claude-sonnet-5`, and context resolution falls back to 200k. A user who adds the
model sees `200k ctx` in `openclaw status` and loses the GA-1M beta-header decision
even though the model is a native 1M-context model. Reported in #99239.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `claude-sonnet-5` where the other GA-1M Anthropic models already live, so the
existing resolution path recognizes it:

- Add the model to both provider lists in the bundled catalog with
  `contextWindow: 1048576` (matching the Opus 4.8 convention and
  `ANTHROPIC_CONTEXT_1M_TOKENS`) and `maxTokens: 128000`.
- Add the single prefix `"claude-sonnet-5"` to both copies of
  `ANTHROPIC_GA_1M_MODEL_PREFIXES`. `startsWith` matching means this one entry
  covers dated (`claude-sonnet-5-20260630`) and dotted (`claude-sonnet-5.0`)
  variants, so no redundant entries are needed.

Scope is limited to catalog data + the prefix constant; no resolution logic
changes. The pre-existing duplication of the prefix list across two files is
untouched here (it is called out in the issue as a separate cleanup).

## User Impact

`claude-sonnet-5` now resolves to its true 1M context window in status output and
GA-1M header logic instead of defaulting to 200k. No behavior change for any other
model.

## Evidence

Regression coverage added to `src/agents/context.test.ts` (the existing GA-1M
table): three rows asserting `resolveContextTokensForModel` returns the fixed 1M
window for `claude-sonnet-5` across `anthropic`, `claude-cli`, and `anthropic-vertex`.
These rows fail before the fix (model resolves to the 200k fallback) and pass after.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `claude-sonnet-5` now resolves to the fixed 1M Anthropic
context window (1048576 for anthropic / claude-cli, 1000000 for anthropic-vertex)
instead of falling back to 200k.

**Environment tested:** Node v24.18.0 on Windows; production TypeScript source
invoked directly via `node --import tsx` against the fix branch.

**Steps run after the patch:** Called the actual patched production functions
`resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow` and `resolveContextTokensForModel` from source,
comparing behavior with and without the prefix entry.

**Evidence after fix:** Before the patch (prefix entry removed), the real function
returns the 200k fallback:

```text
anthropic    claude-sonnet-5 => undefined  (defaults to 200000)
claude-cli   claude-sonnet-5 => undefined  (defaults to 200000)
```

After the patch, `resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow` from source:

```text
anthropic          claude-sonnet-5                => 1048576
anthropic          anthropic/claude-sonnet-5      => 1048576
claude-cli         claude-sonnet-5                => 1048576
anthropic-vertex   claude-sonnet-5                => 1000000
anthropic          claude-sonnet-5-20260630       => 1048576
```

And the wrapper `resolveContextTokensForModel` (the exact rows added to the
regression table):

```text
PASS anthropic        claude-sonnet-5 expected 1048576 got 1048576
PASS claude-cli       claude-sonnet-5 expected 1048576 got 1048576
PASS anthropic-vertex claude-sonnet-5 expected 1000000 got 1000000
ALL REGRESSION ROWS PASS: true
```

Bundled catalog parses and exposes the new entry under both providers:

```text
catalog JSON parses OK
claude-cli sonnet-5 ctx=1048576 max=128000
anthropic  sonnet-5 ctx=1048576 max=128000
```

**Observed result after the fix:** `claude-sonnet-5` is treated as a native 1M model
by the resolver on all three Anthropic providers; the bundled catalog lists it with
`contextWindow: 1048576`.

**Not tested:** A live `openclaw status` render against a running gateway with a real
Anthropic account was not exercised; verification was against the production
resolution functions and the bundled catalog only.

Closes #99239

target.title: improve(gateway): restart only the changed account on channel config reload
target.body:
Related: #99311

## What Problem This Solves

On gateways running multiple accounts on one channel, any config change scoped to a
single account (adding an account, or editing `channels.{kind}.accounts.{accountId}.*`)
restarts the whole channel — every other account on it is disconnected and reconnected
even though their config did not change. On a 9-account Mattermost gateway, each
account-scoped write bounced all connected accounts for 1.0–2.6s and inflated
`config.patch` latency 3–4× during the restart window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reload plan now distinguishes account-scoped paths from channel-global paths. When
all of a channel's changed paths are under `channels.{kind}.accounts.{accountId}[.*]`,
the executor restarts just those `(channel, accountId)` pairs through the existing
`stopChannel`/`startChannel` `accountId` parameter. Any channel-global path keeps the
wholesale restart, and a channel scheduled for wholesale restart drops its per-account
entries, so each `(channel, account)` pair restarts at most once per plan. An account
id the plugin does not list for the new config (removed, renamed, or a config key the
plugin canonicalizes differently — e.g. Matrix's `normalizeAccountId`) promotes that
channel back to a wholesale restart, which already handles stale-account eviction and
non-canonical keys. Per-account restarts mirror the wholesale path's semantics:
non-manual stops (`{ manual: false }`, so a stop timeout does not suppress recovery
scheduling), the same `abortGeneration` guard so an in-process restart is not raced,
and collect-failures-and-continue so one account's failure does not skip the rest of
the plan. `secrets.reload` (server-aux-handlers) has no per-account restart path, so
account-scoped plan entries restart their whole channel there — identical to its
behavior before this change. Malformed account paths (empty account segment) fall
back to wholesale restart. No changes to channel plugins; single-account gateways
keep equivalent behavior.

The default account (`accounts.default.*`) stays on the wholesale path: its config
subtree is the inheritance base other accounts resolve from
(`resolveChannelAccountConfig`), so changing it can affect every account. No existing
tests are modified — the pre-existing whatsapp per-account test (which uses `default`)
keeps its wholesale expectation, correctly. A plan combining a plugin reload with
purely account-scoped channel changes still defers for active work before restarting
accounts.

## User Impact

Operators running many accounts on one channel (multi-account/multi-tenant gateways)
no longer see every account disconnect when one account is added or changed. An
account-scoped reload completes in 0.2–0.7s and touches only that account.
Single-account deployments see no behavior change.

## Evidence

Side-by-side A/B on the same host (`2026.7.1-beta.1`), same gateway, sequentially
mounting 9 Mattermost accounts. Change ported to `main` for this PR: `pnpm build`
and `pnpm check` pass; the touched surface (`config-reload`, `server-reload-handlers`,
`server-aux-handlers`) is 271/271 green. Full `pnpm test` shows a handful of failures
in unrelated files (`model-compat`, `models-config.providers.moonshot`,
`media-understanding/image`) that reproduce identically on pristine `origin/main`
when tests run after `pnpm build` (they pass on a fresh checkout before building) —
a pre-existing post-build state interaction, not introduced here.

| | wholesale (before) | per-account (after) |
|---|---|---|
| restarts per account-add | whole channel | 1 account |
| other-account disconnects | all accounts, 1.0–2.6s per add (45 auto-restarts across 9 mounts) | none |
| reload completion | 0.45–1.5s | 0.18–0.7s |
| `config.patch` latency during reload | 3.3–4.9s worst | ≤2.4s worst |
| failures | none | none |

Before — one account's config write restarts everyone (8 other accounts bounce):

```
[gateway/channels] restarting mattermost channel
```

This adds a narrow request-sender seam while preserving the existing `GatewaySession` constructor path, then covers the urgent behavior directly:

target.title: fix: [Bug]: Control UI approval window closes with queued approvals pending
target.body:
## Summary

Fix a Control UI bug where resolving one queued exec/plugin approval could leave the reused `openclaw-modal-dialog` element's underlying `<dialog>` closed instead of showing the next queued approval. The root cause is that `openclaw-modal-dialog` only opened the dialog in `firstUpdated()` and tracked an internal `opened` boolean latch. When the same custom element was reused with new properties/slot content (queue shift), `firstUpdated()` did not fire again and `openDialog()` returned early because `opened` was already `true`.

The fix adds an `updated()` lifecycle hook that re-evaluates the dialog state on every property-driven render, and changes the `openDialog()` guard from the private `this.opened` latch to the native `dialog.open` property.

Fixes #98379

## Changes

**File:** `ui/src/ui/components/modal-dialog.ts` (+8, -11, net -3)

1. **Added `updated()` lifecycle hook** — calls `openDialog()` after every property-driven render so the dialog re-opens if it was closed.
2. **Changed `openDialog()` guard** — from `if (this.opened)` to `if (!dialog || dialog.open)`, gating on the actual `<dialog>` element state instead of a one-shot latch. Removed redundant inner `dialog.open` checks.

**File:** `ui/src/ui/components/modal-dialog.test.ts` (+46) — added 2 regression tests covering the reuse/reopen scenario.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: After resolving one queued approval prompt, the Control UI approval window now stays open and displays the next pending approval.

**Evidence type**: terminal

**Real setup tested**:
- Runtime: Node v24.13.1, Linux x86_64
- Vitest v4.1.8 with jsdom environment
- Dialog polyfill matches native `<dialog>` behavior

**Exact steps or command run after fix**:
```bash
$ corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.config.ts --project ui \
  src/ui/components/modal-dialog.test.ts \
  src/ui/views/exec-approval.test.ts \
```

**After-fix evidence**:

## Tests and validation

|-----------|-------|--------|

target.title: fix(cli): bound batch-file read size in config-set-input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `--batch-file` path in `parseBatchSource()` at `src/cli/config-set-input.ts` reads an unbounded `fs.readFileSync()` when processing user-specified batch files. A user that accidentally passes a very large file (e.g., a multi-GB log instead of a config batch JSON) will trigger Node to buffer the entire payload, causing OOM pressure. The `--stdin` path in `config-cli.ts` and `exec-approvals-cli.ts` already have 1 MB bounds (`CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`, `EXEC_APPROVALS_STDIN_MAX_BYTES`), but the `--batch-file` path had no equivalent guard.

This is a defense-in-depth fix: in practice batch files for `openclaw config set --batch-file` are small JSON arrays of config entries, but an unbounded disk read from a user-specified path is a standard OOM surface.

## Changes

- Define `MAX_BATCH_FILE_BYTES = 52_428_800` (50 MB) in `config-set-input.ts`. This is deliberately higher than the 1 MB stdin limits because batch files on disk can be larger than typed piped input, while 50 MB still safely prevents OOM from accidentally reading multi-GB files. No real `--batch-file` workload produces a 50 MB JSON config array.
- Replace the unbounded `fs.readFileSync()` with a bounded `fs.openSync()` + `fs.readSync()` that allocates a buffer of `MAX_BATCH_FILE_BYTES + 1` and reads at most that many bytes. If the read fills the buffer beyond the limit, a descriptive error is thrown. This caps memory for all inputs, including special files like `/dev/zero` whose `stat.size` is 0 but produce unbounded reads.
- Open the batch file with `O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK` on POSIX so that FIFOs (named pipes) without a writer are discovered by the `fstat.isFile()` check rather than blocking the CLI indefinitely at `openSync`. On Windows `O_NONBLOCK` is not available and the open falls back to `O_RDONLY` with no behavioral change.
- Add focused regression tests: oversized rejection, exact-limit boundary acceptance with valid parsed assertion, empty-file parse error, FIFO (named pipe) rejection without blocking.
- Preserve all existing behavior: valid files under the limit continue to parse through the same `parseBatchEntries()` path.
- Update CLI `--help` text to advertise the cap.

## Why 50 MB, not 1 MB

The `--stdin` paths are capped at 1 MB because stdin input is typed directly and has no reason to exceed that. Batch files on disk (`--batch-file`) are a different surface: a config batch with thousands of entries can legitimately be larger than 1 MB. Setting the same tight cap would break existing users. 50 MB is a safe defense-in-depth ceiling — a JSON config array of that size (~500K individual entries) far exceeds any real use case — while eliminating the compatibility concern.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: An oversized `--batch-file` must be rejected before parsing with a `Batch file too large` error. A normal-sized (valid) batch file must continue to parse as before. A FIFO (named pipe) path must not block the CLI and must be rejected with a parse error.
- **Real environment tested**: Local Vitest run on Node v22.22.0, exercising real `fs.openSync`/`readSync`/`closeSync` against real temp files on an ext4 filesystem, **plus** a real `openclaw config set --batch-file` CLI invocation against actual batch files, **plus** a real POSIX FIFO proving the nonblocking open prevents indefinite blocking.
- **Exact steps**: 
  1. `pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts` — 13 tests pass including the new oversized-file regression, the exact-limit boundary test with valid payload assertion, and the FIFO nonblocking-open regression.
  2. `node openclaw.mjs config set --batch-file <file> --dry-run` — three scenarios (valid, oversized, empty).
- **Observed result**: All 13 tests pass. Real CLI behavior confirms the bounded read works end-to-end:

  ```
  $ node openclaw.mjs config set --batch-file batch-valid.json --dry-run
  Dry run successful: 3 update(s) validated against $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/openclaw.json.

  $ node openclaw.mjs config set --batch-file batch-oversized.json --dry-run
  Error: Batch file too large: /tmp/batch-oversized.json (max 52,428,800 bytes / 50 MB)

  $ node openclaw.mjs config set --batch-file batch-empty.json --dry-run
  Error: Failed to parse --batch-file: SyntaxError: JSON5: invalid end of input at 1:1
  ```

## Evidence

Focused Vitest:

```
$ pnpm test src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts

```

target.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): resolve stable execPath for worker fork to survive Homebrew Node upgrades
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After Homebrew upgrades Node (e.g. `node 26.3.0 → 26.4.0`), a running Gateway's `process.execPath` still points at the old deleted Cellar path (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node`). The local embedding worker `fork()` uses this stale path and fails with `ENOENT`, silently degrading semantic memory until the gateway is restarted.

## Root Cause

`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts:236` calls `fork()` without an explicit `execPath` option. Node.js's `fork()` defaults to `process.execPath`, which resolves to the real Homebrew Cellar path — not the stable `/opt/homebrew/opt/node/bin/node` symlink. When `brew upgrade` removes the old Cellar directory, every new worker fork hits ENOENT.

## Summary

**Problem**: After Homebrew upgrades Node, the running Gateway's `process.execPath` still points at the old deleted Cellar path. The worker `fork()` uses this stale path and fails with ENOENT, silently degrading semantic memory.

**Solution**: Pre-resolve a stable Node executable path before `fork()`. When `process.execPath` matches a Homebrew Cellar pattern, resolve to the stable opt symlink that survives upgrades. On all other platforms return the original path unchanged.

What changed: New `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` helper (module-level, exported for testing) with a promise cache. `ensureChild()` made async to call the helper before `fork()`. Re-check `this.child?.connected` after async yield to prevent concurrent restart race. New test file with 8 unit tests.

What did NOT change: Public API (`createLocalEmbeddingWorkerProvider`) signature. Package boundaries — no cross-package imports. Worker IPC protocol. Non-Homebrew platform behavior.

## Change Summary

1. **New `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` helper** — module-level, exported for testing. Detects Homebrew Cellar paths (`<prefix>/Cellar/<formula>/<version>/bin/node`) and resolves to the stable opt symlink. Uses lazy module-scoped promise cache.

2. **`ensureChild()` made async** — calls `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` before `fork()` and passes the resolved path via the `execPath` option.

3. **New test file** — 8 unit tests covering Cellar/non-Cellar paths, versioned formulas, opt/bin fallback, cache behavior, and API contract preservation.

### Files changed

- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker.ts` — core fix (+1 import, +1 async modifier, ~45 new LOC)
- `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker-stable-execpath.test.ts` — new tests (~240 LOC)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Prevent local embedding worker fork failure (ENOENT) after Homebrew Node upgrade by resolving a stable execPath before fork().

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64 (Node v24.1.0 via nvm). Homebrew-specific path resolution validated via unit tests with mocked fs.access. Function returns process.execPath unchanged on non-Homebrew platforms, confirming zero regression risk.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Direct function call:
```bash
# node execpath-evidence.ts to verify resolveStableWorkerExecPath() on Linux
process.execPath:      /home/user/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.1.0/bin/node
resolvedWorkerExecPath: /home/user/.config/nvm/versions/node/v24.1.0/bin/node
Match (no regression):  ✅ returns process.execPath unchanged on Linux
Second call returns same: ✅ (cache works)
```

Regex validation:
```bash
# node regex validation — Homebrew Cellar paths matched, others rejected
✅ Homebrew Cellar "/opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/26.3.0/bin/node" → match
✅ Versioned formula "/usr/local/Cellar/node@22/22.11.0/bin/node" → match
✅ Linux "/usr/bin/node" → no match (correct)
✅ Windows "C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe" → no match (correct)
```

New unit tests:
```bash
# pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings-worker-stable-execpath.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
```

Regression tests:
```bash
# pnpm test packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/embeddings.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

Type check:
```bash
# pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:extensions
[tsgo] passed
```

BEFORE FIX: `fork()` called without `execPath` option — defaults to `process.execPath` (stale Homebrew Cellar path after upgrade). After brew upgrade deletes the old binary, each fork fails with ENOENT.

AFTER FIX: `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` checks if `process.execPath` is a Homebrew Cellar path, resolves to stable opt symlink, and passes it via `execPath`. Non-Cellar paths return unchanged. Promise cache prevents repeated fs.access.

**After-fix evidence**:
- Direct function call: `resolveStableWorkerExecPath()` returns `process.execPath` unchanged on Linux (no regression)
- New tests: 8/8 pass covering Cellar, non-Cellar, versioned formula, cache, API backward compat
- Regression tests: 18/18 existing tests pass
- Type check: `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` both pass
- Regex validation: Homebrew Cellar paths correctly matched, non-Cellar paths correctly rejected

**Observed result after the fix**: All 8 new tests pass. All 18 existing regression tests pass. Type check passes. Direct function call on Linux returns `process.execPath` unchanged, proving zero behavior change on non-Homebrew platforms. The fix deterministically resolves a stable execPath before fork(), eliminating the ENOENT failure path from stale Homebrew Cellar binaries.

**What was not tested**: Homebrew Cellar→opt symlink resolution on a real macOS environment (this is Linux CI); this is covered by unit tests that mock `fs.access` behavior. Gateway E2E with actual Node upgrade; the fix only changes `execPath` before `fork()`, the fork+IPC lifecycle is unchanged. Long-running Gateway with repeated worker restarts; the cache test confirms repeat calls use the cached promise.

## Risk checklist

- [ ] **merge-risk**: Low — additive change in a single package (memory-host-sdk), no public API changes, no config changes, no dependency changes. The new helper is an internal detail that only affects one call site (`ensureChild()`). On non-Homebrew platforms the behavior is identical.
- [x] **code change is self-contained**: Yes — ~45 LOC in one file + test file
- [x] **does not affect any public API surface**: Yes — `createLocalEmbeddingWorkerProvider` signature unchanged
- [x] **does not affect any provider/auth/model/catalog code**: Yes
- [x] **does not affect any config/env/defaults surface**: Yes
- [x] **does not affect any channel/plugin/extension code**: Yes
- [x] **proof type**: L2 (direct function call + regex validation + test output)
- [x] **changelog needed**: No — internal implementation detail
- [x] **risk mitigation**: Tests cover all resolution paths; cache prevents repeated fs.access; non-Cellar paths return process.execPath unchanged; no new dependencies introduced; re-check `this.child?.connected` after async yield prevents concurrent restart race

## Test plan

| Scenario | Coverage |
|----------|----------|
| Non-Cellar path (Linux `/usr/bin/node`) | ✅ returns original path unchanged |
| Cellar path + opt symlink exists | ✅ resolves to opt symlink |
| Opt absent + bin symlink exists (default formula) | ✅ falls back to bin symlink |
| All symlinks absent | ✅ returns original execPath |
| Versioned formula `node@22` | ✅ resolves versioned formula; skips bin fallback |
| Cache hit on repeated calls | ✅ caches resolved path |
| API backward compatibility | ✅ provider creation contract preserved |
| Direct call on Linux | ✅ returns process.execPath (no regression) |
| Regex path pattern | ✅ matches Cellar, rejects non-Cellar paths correctly |

## Linked context

- Fixes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99183
- Existing stable-node-path helper: `src/infra/stable-node-path.ts`
- Prior attempt: PR #99222 (ENOENT retry — superseded by this pre-resolution approach)

target.title: test: cover Android main activity lifecycle gates
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android `MainActivity` lifecycle wiring had little focused coverage around the gates that defer initial intents until ViewModel activation, route new intents after activation, and attach runtime UI/service side effects only once after runtime startup.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extracts the lifecycle decisions into small package-internal helpers and covers the urgent behavior without launching the full Compose Activity:

- initial intents are deferred until activation and consumed once
- newer intents received before activation replace the stale pending intent
- intents received after activation route immediately
- runtime UI attachment and foreground service start only once when runtime initialization becomes ready
- the native i18n inventory is synchronized after moving the `OPENCLAW` source line

The Activity still owns the actual ViewModel, Compose, runtime UI, and service calls; the helpers only make the existing gating rules directly testable. The branch is rebased on the upstream reply-init fixture stabilization from #99212 instead of carrying a duplicate core-test patch.

## User Impact

Future Android startup changes are less likely to drop assistant launch intents, replay stale intents, or duplicate runtime UI/service startup work around Activity lifecycle transitions.

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{

  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",

    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],

      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",

      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text

codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.

target.title: docs(memory): align descriptors and docs with recursive memory/**/*.md
target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```

[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY

    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===

```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
{ cfg, agentId: first.agentId });
  const result = await runEmbeddedPiAgent({
    sessionId: runId,
    sessionKey: `agent:${first.agentId}:commitments:${runId}`,
    agentId: first.agentId,
    trigger: "manual",
    sessionFile: resolveExtractionSessionFile(first.agentId, runId),
    workspaceDir: resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, first.agentId),
    config: cfg,
    provider: modelRef.provider,
    model: modelRef.model,
    prompt: buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt({ cfg, items: params.items }),
    disableTools: true,
    thinkLevel: "off",
    verboseLevel: "off",
    reasoningLevel: "off",
    // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
    // commitments extraction inherit the configured fast-mode state (which
    // defaults to false). Hardcoding true caused MiniMax Coding Plans without
    // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
    // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
~~~

target.title: fix(qa-lab): bound suite runtime gateway JSON response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.ts` used an unbounded
`await response.json()` on the gateway HTTP success path inside `fetchJson`.
A misbehaving or hostile gateway endpoint (or accidental huge payload) could
stream oversized JSON and trigger unbounded allocation during `JSON.parse`
while QA Lab suite scenarios read config snapshots or apply config patches
over the local gateway transport.

Replacing the success read with `readProviderJsonResponse` caps JSON parsing at
16 MiB and emits labeled errors such as
`qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`.

This aligns QA Lab's suite runtime gateway with the broader OpenClaw
response-limit campaign that already bounded sibling provider and channel
surfaces (Telegram plugin Bot API reads, Copilot token exchange, Google OAuth,
QA Lab Telegram live transport, etc.).

## Changes

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.ts`:
  - imports `readProviderJsonResponse` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/provider-http`
  - replaces `await response.json()` with
    `readProviderJsonResponse(response, "qa-lab-suite-fetch-json")` in
    `fetchJson`

* `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.test.ts`:
  - adds regression test `bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses` using a
    real `Response` object and asserting the labeled cap error

* `scripts/proof-qa-lab-suite-gateway-bound.mjs`:
  - path-level proof over `node:http` streaming gateway envelopes plus vitest
    regression hook

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Oversized gateway JSON success bodies fail closed
instead of unbounded `JSON.parse` allocation on the QA Lab suite runtime
gateway path.

**Real environment tested:** Node v22.22.0, macOS 15.3.1, `node:http` streaming
server on `127.0.0.1`, built helper from `dist/plugin-sdk/provider-http.js`.

**Exact steps:**
1. Stream an ~18 MiB gateway `{ payload: ... }` envelope from a local HTTP
   server (no `Content-Length`).
2. Drive `readProviderJsonResponse` with label `qa-lab-suite-fetch-json` → assert
   labeled parse cap.
3. Drive the same helper on a buffered >16 MiB envelope (post-fetch handoff shape).
4. Verify a normal config snapshot envelope still parses.
5. Negative control: unbounded `response.json()` on a 64×1 MiB injected stream
   consumes all chunks without canceling.
6. Bounded helper cancels early on the same injected stream.
7. Run qa-lab vitest regression via `fetchJson("http://127.0.0.1:43123/config")`.

**Observed result:**
- Parse boundary (stream): `qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes`
- Buffered oversized envelope: 16 778 254 bytes rejected before `JSON.parse`
- Normal config snapshot envelope parses with hash intact
- Negative control: unbounded `.json()` read all 64 chunks; bounded helper stopped at
  readCount=17 and invoked `cancel()`
- `ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED`

**What was not tested:** live QA Lab suite runs against a real OpenClaw gateway process.

## Evidence

```
=== QA Lab suite gateway bound proof (path-level) ===
--- Case 1: oversized streamed gateway body rejected at parse boundary ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejects oversized streamed gateway body
  ok: parse-boundary label present (got: qa-lab-suite-fetch-json: JSON response exceeds 16777216 bytes)

--- Case 2: oversized buffered gateway envelope (production handoff) ---
  ok: buffered oversized gateway body rejected before JSON.parse
  ok: body size 16778254 bytes exceeds 16777216 cap

--- Case 3: normal gateway config snapshot still parses ---
  ok: config snapshot envelope parses
  ok: config object intact

--- Case 4: negative control — unbounded response.json() ---
  ok: unbounded .json() consumed all 64 chunks (readCount=64)
  ok: stream NOT cancelled via .cancel()

--- Case 5: bounded helper cancels oversized injected stream ---
  ok: readProviderJsonResponse rejected oversized injected stream
  ok: stream read stopped early (readCount=17)
  ok: stream cancel() was invoked

--- Case 6: qa-lab suite gateway regression test ---
  Tests  1 passed | 12 skipped (13)
  ok: vitest qa-lab suite gateway bound regression test passed

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS PASSED
```

```
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test \
  extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-gateway.test.ts \
  -t "bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses"
# Tests  1 passed | 12 skipped (13)
```

New bound regression test (1 added):
- `bounds oversized suite gateway JSON responses` ✓

target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
